stories.title: Himachal Pradesh's monsoon death toll climbs to 157 as floods and landslides batter the state
stories.what_happened: Himachal Pradesh's disaster management authorities confirmed the monsoon death toll has reached **157** between **June 30 and August 9**, with **257 people injured**. The state government put the cost of property damage — roads, bridges, homes and infrastructure — at roughly **₹886 crore**. Officials broke down the causes of death: **89 people died in road accidents** linked to landslide-damaged or washed-out roads, while **68 deaths** came from landslides, drowning, snakebites and falls, reflecting how monsoon hazards compound each other in hill terrain. The India Meteorological Department has **five districts under an orange alert** (meaning be prepared, significant weather expected), and separately warned of **isolated extremely heavy rainfall over East Rajasthan** on August 11. The toll sits within a larger national picture: monsoon-driven floods and landslides have killed **more than 100 people across India since July**, with Assam (about 87 dead) and Kerala (15 dead, 7 missing) also badly affected.
key_points: **157 people have died** and **257 injured** in Himachal Pradesh since the monsoon began on **June 30**.
Property damage is estimated at **₹886 crore** (about $107 million) so far this season.
**Five districts** are currently under an **orange alert** from the India Meteorological Department.
Of the deaths, **89 were from road accidents** and **68 from landslides, drowning, snakebites and falls**.
It adds to a wider national toll — monsoon floods and landslides have killed **over 100 people across India since July**, with Assam and Kerala also hit hard.

depth.background: Himachal Pradesh's hilly terrain makes it especially vulnerable during the **June–September monsoon**: heavy rain triggers landslides on unstable slopes and turns mountain roads treacherous, while flash floods can hit narrow river valleys with little warning. India's monsoon delivers roughly **70% of the country's annual rainfall** and is essential for agriculture, but a monsoon that is unusually intense in a short window — rather than steady over the season — tends to produce this kind of destructive flooding and landslide activity.

stories.title: Ravindra Jadeja returns from career-threatening elbow injury as India name Test squad for Sri Lanka; Bumrah ruled out
stories.what_happened: India's selection committee announced a 15-member Test squad for the tour of Sri Lanka, confirming Ravindra Jadeja's return to the setup for the first time since his **tennis elbow injury in May** ended his involvement in India's home international season. Jadeja had been out of the frame for months as he recovered; his selection now signals selectors are confident in his fitness ahead of two Tests starting August 15 in Galle. In a late change, **Jasprit Bumrah, initially named in the squad, was ruled out because of injury**, a blow to India's pace attack for the series. **KL Rahul was confirmed as vice-captain** to Shubman Gill, and uncapped all-rounder **Saransh Jain**, a standout performer in India's domestic first-class competition, earned a **maiden Test call-up**. The squad announcement follows a build-up in which Gill himself had faced fitness questions over a finger injury sustained in practice, since resolved.
key_points: **Ravindra Jadeja** returns to India's Test squad for the first time since a **tennis elbow injury** sidelined him in May.
**Jasprit Bumrah** was originally picked but has now been **ruled out through injury**.
**KL Rahul** is named **vice-captain** under Test skipper **Shubman Gill**.
Uncapped all-rounder **Saransh Jain** earns a **maiden Test call-up** after strong domestic form.
The two-match series opens in **Galle on August 15**, with the second Test in Colombo.

depth.background: Jadeja is one of India's most important players — a left-arm spinner and lower-order batter whose all-round skill lets India field a more balanced, attacking XI, especially on the slow, turning pitches typical of the subcontinent. He injured his elbow in May 2026 and hasn't played for India since a January ODI against New Zealand, missing several months of international cricket during his recovery. Bumrah, India's premier fast bowler, has been managed carefully through injury in recent years given how central he is to India's pace attack. Shubman Gill leads India's Test side, with the squad for this tour finalized just days before the series begins.

stories.title: BSE to replace Wipro in the Nifty 50 from September 30, in a first for an Indian stock exchange
stories.what_happened: NSE Indices announced BSE will replace Wipro in the Nifty 50 effective the close of business September 29, with the change reflected from September 30, 2026. BSE qualified under NSE's index-entry buffer rule because its six-month average free-float market capitalisation of **₹1,40,879 crore** is at least 1.5 times that of Wipro, the current smallest constituent at **₹55,930 crore**. Wipro drops into the Nifty Next 50 index instead. Index-tracking funds will need to rebalance their holdings to match the new composition, with analysts estimating roughly **$741 million** of inflows into BSE shares and about **$246 million** of outflows from Wipro. The same reshuffle also swaps several Nifty Next 50 constituents, adding Hitachi Energy India, Polycab India, Vedanta Aluminium Metal, and Vodafone Idea.
key_points: **BSE Ltd**, the stock exchange operator, will enter the **Nifty 50** — India's flagship 50-stock index — replacing IT major **Wipro**.
The change takes effect from **September 30, 2026**, following NSE Indices' routine semi-annual reshuffle.
BSE qualified because its free-float market cap of **₹1,40,879 crore** is at least 1.5x Wipro's **₹55,930 crore**.
Analysts estimate roughly **$741 million** of passive-fund inflows into BSE shares and **$246 million** of outflows from Wipro.
It's the **first time** India's own stock exchange operator has entered the marquee index.

depth.background: The **Nifty 50** is India's most-tracked equity index, underlying trillions of rupees in index funds, ETFs, and derivatives contracts. Twice a year, NSE Indices reviews the index and swaps out constituents that fall too far behind on free-float market value — forcing large, mechanical buying and selling by passive funds regardless of a company's underlying business performance. Wipro is a legacy IT-services giant that has lagged its peers in recent years, while BSE has surged in value as India's multi-year retail trading boom has re-rated exchange and broking businesses.

stories.title: West Indies miss direct qualification for the 2027 ODI World Cup for the third straight time
stories.what_happened: Afghanistan beat Ireland by 92 runs in a rain-affected second ODI at Bready Cricket Club, Belfast, clinching the eighth and final automatic World Cup qualification spot alongside defending champions Australia, India, New Zealand, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, England, and Bangladesh. West Indies sit 10th in the ICC ODI rankings and still have two ODIs against India before the September 30 cutoff, but even winning both would not be enough to climb into the top 8. Co-hosts South Africa and Zimbabwe (with Namibia as a third venue) qualify automatically as tournament hosts regardless of ranking. West Indies will now have to navigate a qualifier tournament in **February 2027** just to reach the 14-team, 57-match main event.
key_points: West Indies' hopes of **direct qualification** for the 2027 ODI World Cup are mathematically over.
**Afghanistan's** series-clinching win over Ireland took the last automatic qualification spot, confirmed in reports through **August 10-11**.
The top **8** ODI-ranked teams as of **September 30, 2026** qualify directly; West Indies sit **10th** and can't climb high enough even with two games left against India.
It's the **third consecutive World Cup** the two-time champions (1975, 1979) must reach via a qualifier, set for **February 2027**.
The 2027 World Cup will be co-hosted by **South Africa, Zimbabwe, and Namibia** — the first time it's held in Africa.

depth.background: West Indies won the first two Cricket World Cups ever played, in 1975 and 1979, and were once cricket's dominant force, but the men's ODI team has declined sharply over the past decade. They also missed direct qualification for the 2023 World Cup and had to win a qualifying tournament just to reach that event. Qualification for 2027 is based on each team's ICC ODI ranking as of a set cutoff date, with the top 8 teams (excluding co-hosts) going through automatically.

stories.title: IPL wicketkeeper Abhishek Porel arrested in rape and blackmail case
stories.what_happened: Mogra police in West Bengal's Hooghly district arrested Porel on Tuesday, August 11, and produced him before a court in Chinsurah. The arrest followed a July 20 Calcutta High Court order that directed police to arrest him 'immediately' and seize his electronic devices to protect the complainant's privacy — a directive police took roughly three weeks to act on. The complainant alleges Porel took her to his flat in Mankundu and had a physical relationship with her on the promise of marriage, and that he later denied the relationship and threatened to circulate intimate images and videos of her. Police have registered the case under multiple sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita — India's criminal code — covering sexual offences, plus sections of the IT Act covering privacy violation and image-based blackmail. Porel denies the allegations.
key_points: **Delhi Capitals and Bengal** wicketkeeper-batter **Abhishek Porel**, 23, was arrested by West Bengal police on **August 11, 2026**.
The arrest followed a **Calcutta High Court order** directing police to act 'immediately' and seize his electronic devices.
A medical student alleges a **3.5-year relationship**, a physical relationship on the promise of marriage, and that Porel later threatened to circulate intimate images.
He's charged under multiple sections of the **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita** plus **IT Act** provisions covering privacy violation and blackmail.
Delhi Capitals **retained Porel for ₹4 crore** (about $480,000) for IPL 2026; the franchise had not commented as of the arrest.

depth.background: Porel is a young wicketkeeper-batter who plays for Delhi Capitals in the **Indian Premier League (IPL)** — India's richest domestic T20 competition — and for Bengal in domestic cricket. The complaint was originally lodged in June by a third-year medical student from Karnataka, who says the pair met in January 2023 and were in a relationship for roughly three-and-a-half years, including trips abroad together, before Porel denied the relationship and allegedly threatened to circulate intimate photos and videos of her.

stories.title: IPL stars Klaasen, Miller and Finn Allen sign on for ILT20's star-studded fifth season
stories.what_happened: The DP World ILT20 confirmed a wave of high-profile signings ahead of its fifth season, running **November 22 to December 20, 2026**. South Africa's Heinrich Klaasen and David Miller — both established IPL performers — will make their ILT20 debuts, having signed with Gulf Giants. New Zealand's Finn Allen also debuts in the tournament, joining Abu Dhabi Knight Riders. Australian allrounder Marcus Stoinis returns to the league after a three-year absence to play for Dubai Capitals, which also retained Rovman Powell and Mustafizur Rahman. MI Emirates locked in key players including Nicholas Pooran, Rashid Khan and Romario Shepherd, and added Sherfane Rutherford.
key_points: South Africa's **Heinrich Klaasen** and **David Miller** will make their **ILT20 debuts**, both signed by Gulf Giants.
New Zealand's **Finn Allen** also debuts in the league, joining **Abu Dhabi Knight Riders**.
Australia's **Marcus Stoinis** returns to ILT20 after **three years away**, signing with Dubai Capitals.
The UAE's **DP World ILT20** season 5 runs **November 22 to December 20, 2026**.
Franchises like **MI Emirates** have also locked in key retentions, including **Rashid Khan** and **Nicholas Pooran**.

depth.background: The **ILT20** is the UAE's franchise T20 league, launched in 2023 as a winter alternative for global T20 stars during cricket's packed calendar, competing with leagues like South Africa's SA20 and the Caribbean's CPL for the same pool of players. Teams build squads through a mix of retentions from prior seasons and fresh auctions or signings, similar to the IPL model. All these players are established IPL performers, so their arrival raises the league's profile and viewership potential.

stories.title: Syrian court sentences Bashar al-Assad and his brother to death in absentia for war crimes
stories.what_happened: A Syrian court, in a verdict announced live on state television by judge **Fakhareddine al-Aryan**, sentenced Bashar al-Assad to death in absentia on **August 11, 2026** for crimes against humanity and war crimes committed during the civil war. His brother Maher al-Assad, who commanded the Republican Guard and 4th Armored Division, received the same sentence in absentia, as did six other former military and security officials. Atef Najib, a former security chief and Assad's cousin, was present in court and sentenced in person; his forces' 2011 torture of teenagers in Daraa is widely seen as the spark that lit the uprising. President Ahmed al-Sharaa told Reuters from the Damascus presidential palace: 'Syria is a state of law. The law will take its course on all.' Syrians gathered outside the courthouse, chanting and waving flags as the verdict was read.
key_points: A Damascus court sentenced ousted president **Bashar al-Assad** to death in absentia for **crimes against humanity and war crimes**.
His brother **Maher al-Assad**, ex-commander of the Republican Guard, was also sentenced to death in absentia, along with **six other officials**.
Former security chief **Atef Najib** — whose men torturing teenagers in Daraa helped spark the 2011 uprising — was sentenced in person.
It's the **first conviction of Assad** since he was toppled in **December 2024** after nearly 14 years of civil war.
Assad remains under **Russian protection in Moscow**; experts say a death sentence makes extradition even less likely.

depth.background: Assad's government answered 2011 Arab Spring protests with brutal crackdowns that spiraled into a **14-year civil war**, marked by chemical weapons attacks, mass detentions, and the notorious **Saydnaya prison**, which survivors called a 'human slaughterhouse.' A rebel coalition led by **Ahmed al-Sharaa** — now Syria's interim president — toppled Assad's five-decade family dynasty in **December 2024**, and Assad fled to Russia. Sharaa's new government has been trying to establish transitional justice and the rule of law in a country still recovering from dictatorship and war.

stories.title: Joe Root returns as England's Test captain for the Pakistan series, after Ben Stokes' shock retirement
stories.what_happened: England's selectors have named Root as captain for at least the first two Tests of a three-match series against Pakistan, with reports suggesting he could stay in charge through next year's Ashes series if things go well. Alongside the captaincy change, the squad has been reshaped by injury and form: **Jacob Bethell**, tipped as a rising middle-order batter, is out with a knee injury, opening a spot for wicketkeeper-batter **Jordan Cox** to bat at No. 3. Experienced batters **Dan Lawrence and Ollie Pope** return to the fold after being out of the side. The series begins August 19 at Headingley, Leeds, followed by Lord's (Aug 27-31) and Edgbaston (Sep 9-13).
key_points: England named a **16-player squad** for the first two Tests against Pakistan, with **Joe Root as captain** — his first time leading the side since **2022**.
Root steps in after **Ben Stokes' sudden retirement** from international cricket, announced mid-match during England's series against New Zealand.
**Jacob Bethell is ruled out** with a right knee injury; **Jordan Cox** is drafted in to bat at No. 3 in his place.
**Dan Lawrence and Ollie Pope** earn recalls to the squad as England rebuild for a **three-Test series starting August 19** at Headingley.

depth.background: Ben Stokes had captained England's Test side since 2022, reshaping the team around an aggressive, fast-scoring style known as "Bazball." His retirement mid-series against New Zealand stunned English cricket, ending a 15-year international career and leaving the captaincy vacant with a major home series against Pakistan just weeks away. Joe Root, England's most capped modern batter and their captain from 2017-2022 before he stepped down for Stokes, was the obvious experienced option to steady the side.

stories.title: Manchester Super Giants crush SunRisers Leeds to move to the brink of a Hundred men's Eliminator spot
stories.what_happened: In the 30th match of the 2026 Hundred men's competition at **Old Trafford, Manchester**, on **August 11**, Manchester Super Giants routed SunRisers Leeds, chasing down their target in just **67 legal balls** thanks to unbeaten innings from **Tim Seifert (80\*)** and **Paul Walter (44\*)**. The result vaulted Super Giants above SunRisers Leeds into second place in the table, putting them on the brink of confirming their place in Friday's Eliminator. **Trent Rockets**, meanwhile, had already secured their place directly in the final by finishing top of the table.
key_points: MSG chased down the target in just **67 legal balls**, a dominant run-chase.
The win moved Super Giants above SunRisers Leeds into **second place** in the table.
**Trent Rockets** have already secured their spot straight in the **final**.
**Tim Seifert (80\* not out)** and **Paul Walter (44\* not out)** anchored the chase.
The men's **Eliminator** is set for **Friday, August 14** at the Kia Oval; the final follows at Lord's on **August 16**.

depth.background: The Hundred is English cricket's short-format franchise competition, with eight men's and eight women's teams playing a round-robin followed by knockouts: the top team goes straight to the final, while the 2nd and 3rd-placed teams meet in an Eliminator for the second final spot. Trent Rockets had already all-but wrapped up top spot heading into the final league games.

stories.title: Nottinghamshire's cricket boss quits for Lancashire less than a year into the job
stories.what_happened: Nottinghamshire County Cricket Club confirmed that chief executive Richard Kenyon is leaving to take up the same role at Lancashire, succeeding Lancashire's departing CEO Daniel Gidney. Kenyon had only joined Nottinghamshire in **December 2025**, making his stint at Trent Bridge just over eight months. He previously spent more than a decade at Everton Football Club in senior commercial and community roles. Nottinghamshire's chairman Andy Hunt said he was disappointed Kenyon was leaving so early in his tenure but understood the appeal of a role closer to Kenyon's home region in the northwest of England. The club has appointed commercial director Michael Temple as interim chief executive while it searches for a permanent replacement.
key_points: Nottinghamshire CEO **Richard Kenyon** is leaving to become Lancashire's new chief executive.
He only joined Notts in **December 2025**, meaning he departs after **barely eight months**.
He replaces outgoing Lancashire CEO **Daniel Gidney**.
Notts chairman **Andy Hunt** said he's 'disappointed' but understands the pull of Kenyon's home region.
Notts' commercial director **Michael Temple** steps in as **interim CEO** at Trent Bridge.

depth.background: Richard Kenyon built his executive career at Everton Football Club, including a lead role delivering its new Bramley-Moore Dock stadium, before moving into cricket administration. English county cricket clubs like Nottinghamshire (based at Trent Bridge) and Lancashire (based at Old Trafford) are run as separate businesses with their own commercial operations, competing for revenue, sponsorships and top staff much like any sports franchise.

stories.title: UAE thrash Canada by 97 runs in World Cup League 2, Rahul Chopra hits unbeaten 127
stories.what_happened: In the **125th match** of League 2, played at **Forthill, Dundee**, the **United Arab Emirates beat Canada by 97 runs**. Batting first, UAE posted **282 for 6** in their 50 overs, built around an **unbeaten 127 from Rahul Chopra**, who was named Player of the Match. Canada's chase never got close, folding for **185** in 33.4 overs. The win strengthens UAE's position in the League 2 standings as the qualification race for the **2027 ODI World Cup** continues.
key_points: **UAE beat Canada by 97 runs** in the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup League 2 in Dundee, Scotland.
UAE posted **282/6** in 50 overs; Canada were bowled out for **185** in 33.4 overs.
**Rahul Chopra** was Player of the Match for an **unbeaten 127**, anchoring UAE's total.
League 2 is a key **qualification pathway** toward the 2027 ODI World Cup for associate nations.

depth.background: **ICC Men's Cricket World Cup League 2** is a multi-year one-day international series that gives cricket's **associate nations** (countries outside the sport's traditional 12 full members, like UAE, Canada, Scotland, Nepal and Oman) a structured route to try to qualify for the next 50-over World Cup, since they don't get automatic entry the way top-ranked teams do. Results across dozens of matches over several years determine which teams advance toward the qualifying tournament.

stories.title: SunRisers Leeds Women stun Manchester Super Giants to set up Hundred eliminator against Southern Brave
stories.what_happened: In a winner-takes-all final group match at Old Trafford, **SunRisers Leeds Women beat Manchester Super Giants Women by 41 runs**, with **Annabel Sutherland's unbeaten 62 off just 36 balls** anchoring Leeds' total. The win means Leeds **leapfrogged Manchester** in the standings and secured second place behind **Trent Rockets**, who had already topped the table on points and qualified directly for the final. Leeds will now play **Southern Brave**, who finished the group stage third, in an **eliminator on August 14**, with the winner advancing to face Trent Rockets in the final.
key_points: **SunRisers Leeds Women** beat **Manchester Super Giants** by **41 runs** in a winner-takes-all group match.
**Annabel Sutherland's unbeaten 62 off 36 balls** powered Leeds' innings.
The reigning champions now face **Southern Brave** in an **eliminator on August 14** for a place in the final.
**Trent Rockets** already topped the women's table and go straight into the final without playing the eliminator.

depth.background: The Hundred is English cricket's short-form franchise competition, played in 100-ball innings, with separate men's and women's tournaments run in parallel across the same eight city-based teams. SunRisers Leeds are the reigning women's champions. With the group stage wrapping up, final places and playoff spots were still being decided by results on the last matchday, making today's Leeds-Manchester match a straight knockout for a shot at the eliminator.

stories.title: Zelensky warns North Korea is turning real battlefield experience against Ukraine into a bigger long-term threat
stories.what_happened: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on August 11 that North Korea's deployment of troops to fight alongside Russia is giving Pyongyang **real modern combat experience** it has never had, and that this is making North Korea a **bigger long-term military threat**. He reiterated earlier estimates that **30,000 to 50,000** North Korean soldiers have been sent to Russia, and said a North Korean **missile unit** — potentially equipped with **120 ballistic missiles and six launchers** — has begun deploying to western Russia for potential strikes on Ukraine. Separately, reporting shows North Korea has delivered roughly **4 million artillery shells** to Russia since mid-2023. The US, meanwhile, has resumed sending Ukraine military supplies, including Patriot air-defense systems funneled through NATO.
key_points: Ukraine's president says fighting alongside Russia is making North Korea's military **stronger and more dangerous**.
Up to **30,000-50,000 North Korean troops** have been deployed to support Russia, per Zelensky's estimates.
A North Korean **missile unit** has begun deploying to western Russia, reportedly with **120 ballistic missiles**.
North Korea has sent **4 million artillery shells** to Russia since mid-2023.
It's Pyongyang's **most significant war involvement since the 1950s** Korean War.

depth.background: North Korea and Russia signed a mutual-defense treaty in June 2024 during Vladimir Putin's visit to Pyongyang, committing each to assist the other if attacked. Since then, North Korea has gone from selling Russia ammunition to sending its own soldiers to fight — first reported in late 2024 — marking the first time North Korean troops have fought a foreign war since 1953. In exchange, Russia is widely believed to be sharing military technology and combat know-how that North Korea has never had access to before.

stories.title: DR Congo's Ebola outbreak becomes the deadliest on record as deaths pass 2,000
stories.what_happened: Congolese health officials confirmed on Tuesday, August 11, that the death toll from the current Ebola outbreak has surpassed **2,000**, out of **4,381** confirmed cases — a case fatality rate of nearly **46%**. The outbreak is concentrated in the DRC's eastern and northeastern regions, areas already destabilized by armed conflict, which makes it harder for health workers to trace contacts and deliver vaccines. Gavi, the global vaccine alliance, has warned this **could become the largest Ebola outbreak ever recorded**. The speed is what alarms epidemiologists most: in a comparable 2018-2020 outbreak, it took over a year to reach 2,000 deaths — this time it happened in under a month once the 1,000 mark was passed.
key_points: **2,011 people have died** and **4,381 cases** are confirmed as of August 11, officials say.
The case fatality rate is **45.9%** — nearly half of everyone infected has died.
Deaths went from 1,000 to 2,000 in **under a month**, far faster than any prior DRC outbreak.
This is the DRC's **17th Ebola surge** and could become the **largest ever recorded**.
The outbreak is centered in **conflict-hit eastern and northeastern** DRC, hampering the response.

depth.background: Ebola is a severe viral hemorrhagic fever spread through contact with bodily fluids, first identified in the DRC (then Zaire) in 1976 near the Ebola River, for which the disease is named. The DRC has more experience fighting Ebola than any country on Earth — this is its **17th outbreak** since then, and a 2018-2020 outbreak that killed over 2,000 people took **more than a year** to reach that toll. This outbreak was declared on 15 May 2026 but is believed to have been silently spreading for weeks before detection, giving it a head start most past outbreaks didn't have.

stories.title: Pakistan told to shield Babar Azam from English media as he returns as Test captain for the Headingley series
stories.what_happened: Ahead of Pakistan's three-Test tour of England, starting August 19 at Headingley, former Pakistan captain and wicketkeeper Rashid Latif said the PCB should **limit Babar Azam's exposure to English media**, arguing that Shan Masood — who has more experience playing county cricket in England — is better placed to front press duties. The comments come as Babar prepares for his first major series back in the captaincy, under scrutiny after Pakistan's poor Test results under Masood. Pakistan's 17-member squad for the series includes four uncapped players: spinner Ali Usman, batter Muhammad Awais Zafar, fast bowler Ubaid Shah, and wicketkeeper-batter Muhammad Ghazi Ghori. The series continues with Tests at Lord's from August 27 and Edgbaston from September 9.
key_points: Former captain Rashid Latif wants the PCB to **limit Babar Azam's media interactions** in England.
Latif argues **Shan Masood**, whom Babar replaced as captain, is better suited to handle English media.
Babar is back as Test captain for a **third stint**, leading the West Indies and England tours.
The **first Test starts August 19 at Headingley**, Leeds, followed by Lord's and Edgbaston.
Pakistan named a 17-member squad including **four uncapped players**.

depth.background: Babar Azam is Pakistan's most prominent modern batter and has held and lost the national captaincy multiple times across formats amid inconsistent results and dressing-room politics. He was replaced as Test captain by Shan Masood in December 2023, a switch that yielded 12 defeats in 16 Tests. In July, the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) reinstated Babar as Test captain ahead of tours to the West Indies and England, his third distinct spell in the role.

stories.title: Houthi missiles kill six in first fatal Red Sea shipping attack in over a year
stories.what_happened: On Tuesday, Houthi forces fired three ballistic missiles at the Tihamah, a small Egyptian-owned cargo vessel carrying food through the Bab al-Mandeb Strait off Yemen's coast. The initial strike set the ship ablaze and killed four crew members — three Pakistanis and one Indonesian — according to Yemen's Transport Ministry. As Yemen's government-aligned National Resistance Forces launched a rescue operation to evacuate the dead and wounded, the Houthis fired again, striking the rescue site directly in what officials called a **'double-tap' strike**. That second strike killed two more people among the rescue forces, bringing the total dead to six, with at least ten more wounded. Yemen's coast guard and two military officials confirmed the account. Hours earlier and roughly 300 miles away, a US Navy helicopter fired Hellfire missiles to disable the Panama-flagged cargo ship Vela Nova in the Gulf of Oman, after CENTCOM said the vessel tried to breach the US blockade on Iranian ports — the **12th vessel** the US has struck since April.
key_points: Houthi rebels fired **three ballistic missiles** at the cargo ship Tihamah in the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, sparking a fire that killed **four crew members** — three Pakistani nationals and one Indonesian.
As rescuers rushed to evacuate the wounded, the Houthis struck the same site again in a **'double-tap' strike**, killing **two more** rescue workers from Yemen's National Resistance Forces.
The **six deaths** mark the first fatalities from a Houthi attack on Red Sea shipping in **more than a year**, and the first since the US-Israel war on Iran began in late February.
Yemen's government says **ten more people** were wounded in the attack, which set the Egyptian-owned vessel ablaze and caused significant damage.
The strike came the same day US forces disabled a **separate** cargo ship, the Vela Nova, in the nearby Gulf of Oman for allegedly running Washington's naval blockade on Iran.

depth.background: The Houthis are an Iran-aligned armed group that controls most of northern Yemen and has fought a decade-long civil war against Yemen's internationally recognized government. Since late 2023 they have attacked commercial vessels passing through the **Bab al-Mandeb Strait**, a narrow chokepoint at the southern mouth of the Red Sea through which a large share of Europe-Asia trade normally flows, framing the campaign as solidarity with Palestinians in Gaza. Attacks had slowed sharply over the past year as earlier rounds of US and Israeli strikes degraded Houthi capabilities, but tensions have reignited with the wider **US-Israel war on Iran**, which the Houthis back as part of Tehran's regional network of allied militias.

stories.title: Alpine's Franco Colapinto robbed during F1 summer break, deletes post after backlash over his wording
stories.what_happened: Colapinto discovered his car had been broken into and emptied at Lake Como, a popular Italian holiday destination, during the F1 summer shutdown. He shared photos of the missing items — including clothes and his mate-drinking kit, a cultural staple for many Argentines — on social media. His original caption read, roughly, that it was surprising **'Italians would steal everything from a Latino'** and joked the thieves 'won't like the mate,' a comment that read to many as a jab at safety standards in Italy versus Argentina. The post quickly drew criticism online for generalizing about Italians, prompting Colapinto to edit the word to **'Europeans'** before removing the post altogether. No arrests or further details about the theft have been reported, and Alpine has stayed silent on the matter publicly.
key_points: **Franco Colapinto**, Alpine's Argentine driver, was targeted by thieves while holidaying at **Lake Como**, Italy during F1's mandatory summer shutdown.
He had left his luggage inside his car; on returning he found it **completely stripped**, losing clothing and his traditional **mate tea set**.
His first social-media post blamed **'Italians'** for the theft and contrasted it with safety in Argentina, sparking online backlash.
Colapinto edited the wording to **'Europeans'** before **deleting the post entirely**.
**Alpine has not issued an official comment** on the incident as of today.

depth.background: Colapinto, 23, is one of F1's most closely watched young drivers, having broken through with Williams in 2024 before moving to **Alpine** for 2025-26, where he built a large, vocal fanbase, especially in Argentina. Every August, F1 enforces a **mandatory summer shutdown** — a fixed period when all teams must close their factories and stop car development, giving staff and drivers a genuine break mid-season. Colapinto was on personal holiday in northern Italy during this window when the incident occurred.

stories.title: China's Landspace makes its second attempt to catch-land a reusable rocket booster, a SpaceX-style first for a private Chinese firm
stories.what_happened: Landspace has scheduled its Zhuque-3 rocket (Flight 2) to launch from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center and attempt to land its reusable first stage using powered descent and landing legs, targeting **23:45 UTC on August 10** (early morning August 11 in Beijing). The rocket is built from stainless steel and burns methane and liquid oxygen — the same basic recipe SpaceX uses for its next-generation Starship. This is Landspace's **second** attempt at a full catch-landing after its December 2025 debut, in which the vehicle reached orbit successfully but the booster **exploded during its final landing burn**. If successful, it would be the **fourth** orbital-booster-recovery attempt by a Chinese company in 2026 and the first by a private (non-state) Chinese firm using powered landing legs rather than a net or barge capture. The outcome of the attempt was not yet confirmed as of this report.
key_points: Landspace targets a launch-and-landing attempt of its **Zhuque-3** rocket at **23:45 UTC on August 10** from Jiuquan.
It's the company's **second** attempt — its December 2025 debut reached orbit but the booster **exploded during final descent**.
A successful landing would make Landspace the **first private Chinese company** to recover an orbital rocket booster.
China already landed a booster once before, via **net-capture** on a ship in July 2026 — this attempt uses **powered landing legs** instead, like SpaceX's Falcon 9.
Zhuque-3 runs on **stainless steel and methane/liquid-oxygen**, the same propellant combination SpaceX uses for Starship.

depth.background: Reusable rockets matter because **not throwing away the expensive first stage** after every launch is the single biggest reason SpaceX's Falcon 9 cut the cost of reaching orbit by roughly an order of magnitude over the last decade. China has been racing to close that gap: state-linked and private Chinese rocket companies have made several booster-recovery attempts in 2026, with the first confirmed success coming via a **net-capture ship** in July. Landspace, a private Chinese launch company, is trying the harder version — landing on legs using its own engine, the same method SpaceX pioneered — after its first attempt in December 2025 ended when the booster blew up moments before touchdown.

stories.title: Southern Brave end Trent Rockets' 6-match winning streak, denying them an automatic spot in The Hundred final
stories.what_happened: Southern Brave ended Trent Rockets' six-match winning streak at Trent Bridge, denying the hosts automatic passage to The Hundred final with a 6-wicket win. Tristan Stubbs anchored the chase with an unbeaten 52 off just 28 balls, including a six struck off Lewis Gregory to bring up his half-century with three balls to spare, with Marcus Stoinis also contributing to the winning total. In the accompanying women's fixture at the same ground, Trent Rockets Women won by 3 wickets with 2 balls remaining, chasing down Southern Brave Women's total of 117 for 5. The men's result means Trent Rockets, who had been the tournament's standout team through the group stage, now need results elsewhere to go their way, rather than guaranteeing their final spot outright.
key_points: Southern Brave won by **6 wickets**, snapping Trent Rockets' **six-match winning streak**.
Tristan Stubbs hit an unbeaten **52 off 28 balls**, sharing the chase with Marcus Stoinis.
The result denies Trent Rockets **automatic qualification** for Sunday's final.
In the women's match at the same venue, **Trent Rockets won by 3 wickets** with 2 balls to spare.
Trent Rockets had been the form team of **The Hundred's** group stage before this loss.

depth.background: **The Hundred** is England's 100-ball-per-innings franchise cricket tournament, running men's and women's competitions in parallel each August. Teams that finish top of the group-stage table qualify directly for the final; the second- and third-placed teams instead have to win an eliminator match for the second final spot.

stories.title: Trent Rockets Men clinch an automatic Hundred final spot, topping the table on 28 points
stories.what_happened: Trent Rockets Men beat **Southern Brave** on Monday, August 10, in their final group-stage match, finishing on top of the men's Hundred table with **28 points** from their eight matches. Topping the table gives them **automatic qualification for Sunday's final** at Lord's, meaning they skip Friday's eliminator between the second- and third-placed teams entirely. It caps a dominant group stage in which the Rockets won the bulk of their fixtures, having already sealed a top-three finish and a knockout spot earlier in the tournament after beating MI London. The result is separate from — and coincides with — Trent Rockets' **women's** team also finishing top of their own group this week, giving the club a strong showing across both competitions.
key_points: Trent Rockets Men beat **Southern Brave** in their final group match to top the table on **28 points**.
The win secures an **automatic spot in Sunday's final** at Lord's, skipping the eliminator entirely.
It caps the men's team's **strongest-ever Hundred campaign**, capping a dominant group stage.
The men's final is on **August 16**; an eliminator on August 14 decides who joins them.
This is a separate storyline from Trent Rockets' **women's** team, who also topped their own group this week.

depth.background: The Hundred is England's short-format 100-ball cricket competition, running men's and women's tournaments in parallel with matching team names and shared venues. Trent Rockets — based at Trent Bridge, Nottingham — have had contrasting histories in the men's and women's competitions since the tournament launched in 2021. Eight teams compete in each group stage, with the top two advancing straight to the final and the next two playing an eliminator for the remaining final spot.

stories.title: Trent Rockets edge Southern Brave by 6 runs in a tense Hundred thriller at Trent Bridge
stories.what_happened: Trent Rockets posted 133 for 8 in their innings at Trent Bridge today, and then restricted Southern Brave to 127, winning by **6 runs** in a much tighter contest than some of their earlier games this season. The result adds to Rockets' strong campaign, coming after they had already locked up the men's competition's top seed heading into the knockouts. Southern Brave's chase fell just short despite a competitive run total, keeping their own path through the group stage under pressure.
key_points: Trent Rockets posted **133 for 8**, then held on to beat Southern Brave by **6 runs**.
Southern Brave fell short at **127**, unable to chase down the target at Trent Bridge.
The win keeps Rockets' strong campaign going after they'd already **clinched the men's top seed**.
It's a different, tighter contest from Rockets' earlier blowout wins this competition.
The Hundred's knockout stage is approaching, with seeding battles intensifying across the table.

depth.background: The Hundred is England and Wales Cricket Board's short-format (100-balls-per-side) domestic competition, now in its sixth season, designed to draw new and younger audiences to cricket with a fast, TV-friendly format. Trent Rockets have been one of the stronger men's teams this season, having already beaten MI London and secured the competition's top seed for the knockout stage. Southern Brave, meanwhile, has been fighting to stay in contention as the group phase winds down.

stories.title: Parliament passes bill letting government allow charges on UPI payments — Sitharaman says users pay nothing, Opposition unconvinced
stories.what_happened: Parliament passed the **Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026** — the Lok Sabha approved it the previous week, and the **Rajya Sabha cleared it on Monday evening, August 10**, after a brief but heated debate that saw the Opposition walk out. As a Money Bill, the Rajya Sabha could only suggest changes before sending it back to the Lok Sabha. Its most contested provision amends Section 10A of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act to let the central government permit banks and payment providers to levy charges on **UPI and other digital payment modes — a legal power that didn't exist before**. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman told the House this is merely an 'enabling provision,' not an actual fee, and that any future decision on a Merchant Discount Rate (the fee a merchant pays a bank per transaction) would go through NPCI's UPI oversight committee, with consumers and small merchants continuing to pay nothing. Opposition MP Sanjay Singh directly rebutted her, calling the assurance 'contradictory and misleading' — noting she'd earlier floated a committee to decide 'how much tax' to charge traders — and alleged the bill was introduced under **pressure from the US**, whose government has reportedly wanted UPI monetized after Indians shifted away from Visa and Mastercard toward the free system. The bill separately includes unrelated tax breaks for data-centre services and incentives for the diamond-trading industry.
key_points: The **Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026** cleared the Rajya Sabha on **August 10**, after the Lok Sabha passed it the week before.
It amends the payments law to let the government **permit banks and payment firms to charge fees on UPI** for the first time.
Finance Minister **Nirmala Sitharaman** called it only an 'enabling provision' and promised **no charges for consumers or small merchants**.
Opposition MP **Sanjay Singh** called her assurance 'contradictory and misleading' and alleged the bill came under **pressure from the US**.
The bill also adds tax breaks for **data-centre services** and incentives for the **diamond trade**.

depth.background: UPI (Unified Payments Interface) is India's instant, phone-based payment system, run by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI), and has become the backbone of everyday digital payments across the country — from street vendors to online shopping — largely because it has always been **free** for users and merchants. That free-ness has also made UPI a competitive threat to card networks like Visa and Mastercard, whose merchant fees UPI undercuts entirely. Until now, the law governing digital payments had no clause explicitly allowing anyone to charge fees on UPI transactions. This new bill inserts that clause for the first time, even though the government insists it has no immediate plan to use it.

stories.title: Afghanistan lock in a direct spot at the 2027 Cricket World Cup by beating Ireland in their ODI series
stories.what_happened: Afghanistan clinched a spot at the **2027 ICC Cricket World Cup**, to be held in Southern Africa, after taking an unassailable lead in their ODI series against Ireland in Belfast. The turning point was a nerve-wracking **third ODI**, which Afghanistan won by **three wickets** with the match going deep into the final overs; **Rashid Khan** contributed **37 runs** in the chase. The result confirmed Afghanistan's place via **direct qualification** rather than a later qualifying tournament, marking the team's **fourth consecutive World Cup appearance**. The series against Ireland continued afterward, with a fourth ODI played in Belfast on August 12.
key_points: Afghanistan **secured direct qualification for the 2027 ODI Cricket World Cup** in Southern Africa by winning their ODI series against Ireland in Belfast.
The decisive win came in a tense **third ODI**, which Afghanistan won by **three wickets**, giving them an unassailable series lead.
**Rashid Khan** made a crucial **37 runs** to help Afghanistan chase down their target with the match going to the wire.
This is Afghanistan's place at a **fourth consecutive Cricket World Cup**, continuing the team's rapid rise since gaining full ICC membership in 2017.

depth.background: Afghanistan's cricket team has gone from an associate nation to a fixture at global tournaments in under a decade, driven by a generation of players — including star leg-spinner Rashid Khan — who came through refugee camps and a fledgling domestic system before the country had ICC full-member status. Direct qualification for the ODI World Cup goes to a mix of top-ranked teams and designated hosts, with everyone else fighting through a separate qualifying tournament — so securing a direct berth well in advance is a significant marker of how established the team has become. Ireland, meanwhile, remains an associate-turned-full-member side still working to become a consistent threat at the highest level.

stories.title: Turkey's parliament passes a landmark amnesty law for PKK militants, a first legal step after 40 years of conflict
stories.what_happened: Turkey's parliament passed a 12-article bill on Monday that creates a legal pathway for thousands of PKK members to reintegrate into society, following 12 hours of debate and a **468-88** vote with six abstentions. The law suspends some prison sentences and delays ongoing investigations and trials for **5 to 10 years** depending on the severity of the alleged offence, but it explicitly excludes anyone convicted of intentional killings or serving a life sentence handed down before 2005 — a carve-out that keeps Ocalan himself, and other senior commanders, out of its scope. New ministerial and parliamentary committees will monitor the disarmament process, and the law only takes effect once Turkey's National Security Council formally confirms the PKK has disbanded and surrendered its weapons. Once that happens, eligible militants will have **six months** to apply for its protections.
key_points: Lawmakers voted **468 to 88** to pass the 'terror-free Turkey' bill after **12 hours of debate**.
The law offers **conditional amnesty**, not a full pardon, to thousands of PKK fighters who disarm.
It comes **18 months** after jailed PKK founder **Abdullah Ocalan** urged followers to lay down weapons.
Ocalan himself and militants convicted of killings or serving life terms are **excluded** from the law.
Some prison sentences will be suspended and trials postponed for **5 to 10 years**, depending on the offence.

depth.background: The **PKK (Kurdistan Workers' Party)** has fought the Turkish state for roughly **40 years**, seeking greater rights and autonomy for Turkey's Kurdish minority, in a conflict that has killed an estimated 40,000 people. In 2025, Ocalan called on the group to disband, and the PKK responded with a symbolic disarmament ceremony in northern Iraq, withdrawing fighters from Turkey. This week's vote is the Turkish parliament's first concrete legislative step to turn that peace process into law, covering how militants can return to civilian life.

stories.title: Intel plans to sell $15 billion in new stock to fund its AI chip comeback
stories.what_happened: Intel announced on Monday a proposed **$15 billion underwritten public offering of common stock**, with major banks including JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, and Citigroup running the sale. The company said it may grant underwriters a 30-day option to buy an extra **$2.25 billion** in shares if demand is strong. Intel said the money will go toward **capital expenditures and working capital** — chiefly building out chip manufacturing capacity — while preserving its investment-grade credit rating. The announcement cited **strong and sustainable AI-driven demand** for physical AI, custom silicon, advanced packaging, and external wafer manufacturing. Intel shares fell more than 3% premarket on the news, even though the stock has nearly tripled in 2026 to around $101.
key_points: Intel announced a **$15 billion stock offering**, selling new shares to raise cash for chip factories and AI hardware investment.
It may sell up to **$2.25 billion more** if underwriter demand is strong — potentially **$17.25 billion** total.
Intel's stock has **nearly tripled this year** on AI-driven demand, hitting around $101.65, which is what makes raising this much by selling shares attractive now.
The stock still **fell over 3%** on the news, because issuing new shares dilutes existing shareholders.
Intel already raised its 2026 capital-spending target from **$18 billion to $20 billion** in July.

depth.background: Intel has spent the past two years trying to claw back ground lost to Nvidia, AMD, and TSMC in the AI chip race, while also building out its **foundry business** — manufacturing chips for other companies, the way TSMC does. That turnaround has been expensive and has drawn **direct government backing**: the US government took an equity stake in Intel earlier this year as part of efforts to secure domestic chip production. Intel's stock has rallied hard in 2026 on hopes the AI buildout will finally pay off, giving the company a rare window to raise large sums of cash by selling new shares at a high price rather than borrowing.

stories.title: Ireland stun Afghanistan by 6 wickets to level the ODI series, Ed Joyce hits an unbeaten 105
stories.what_happened: In the series decider at Belfast, **Ireland chased down Afghanistan's total with six wickets in hand**, powered by an unbeaten **105 from Ed Joyce**, the standout innings of the match. Kevin O'Brien contributed a brisk 75, and Paul Stirling finished the chase unbeaten on 39, as Ireland comfortably reeled in the target. The win means the three-match series finishes **level at 1-1**, denying Afghanistan the series victory they had been favoured for after their dominant second-match performance. Afghanistan had won the toss and batted first, but their total proved insufficient against Ireland's controlled, senior-player-led chase.
key_points: Ireland beat Afghanistan by **6 wickets** in the 3rd ODI at Belfast, denying Afghanistan a series-clinching win.
**Ed Joyce** anchored the chase with an unbeaten **105**, backed by Kevin O'Brien's 75 and Paul Stirling's unbeaten 39.
The result **levels the three-match series**, after Afghanistan had gone 1-0 up with a dominant win in the 2nd ODI.
The series carried **World Cup qualification points**, making today's result directly relevant to both teams' qualifying hopes.
It reverses the expected script — Afghanistan had been favourites to seal the series after their emphatic 2nd-ODI win.

depth.background: Ireland and Afghanistan have been playing a three-match ODI series in Belfast that carries **ICC World Cup Super League-style qualification points**, meaning results directly affect both teams' paths toward qualifying for the next global tournament. Afghanistan, led by their in-form bowling attack, had gone into the decider with a 1-0 series lead after a dominant win in the second match, putting them in a strong position to close out the series today.

stories.title: Punjab ends decades of outsourced government jobs, moving 26,000-28,000 workers onto direct contracts
stories.what_happened: On the concluding day of its Monsoon Session, the Punjab Vidhan Sabha unanimously passed the **Punjab State Outsourced Personnel (Transition to Contractual Engagement) Bill, 2026**, alongside eight other bills including a GST amendment and a Punjab Protection of Trees Bill. The outsourcing bill applies to eligible Group-C and Group-D employees engaged in essential public services, moving them from third-party outsourcing onto **direct contractual engagement with the government**. It scraps the **15-22% commission** that outsourcing agencies previously deducted from worker pay, redirecting that money to the workers. Affected employees become entitled to **Provident Fund, Employees' State Insurance, gratuity, and maternity and casual leave** — benefits they were previously denied. Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann called it a historic decision, saying the state's decades-old outsourcing system "will come to an end" from Monday. A separate bill on full regularisation of these workers was deferred for further work.
key_points: The Punjab Assembly **unanimously passed** the Punjab State Outsourced Personnel (Transition to Contractual Engagement) Bill, 2026.
It moves **26,000-28,000 outsourced Group-C and Group-D employees** onto direct government contracts.
Workers will now get **Provident Fund, gratuity, ESI, and maternity/casual leave** — benefits outsourced staff previously didn't receive.
The **15-22% commission** private outsourcing agencies used to skim off worker pay will now go to the **workers themselves**.
CM Bhagwant Mann called it a **"historic decision"** ending Punjab's outsourcing system "from today."

depth.background: For years, many government departments in Punjab — like most Indian states — filled essential-service roles (sweepers, drivers, clerks, health-department staff) not through direct hiring but via **private outsourcing agencies**. Those agencies were paid by the government but took a **cut of 15-22%** as commission before passing on wages, and outsourced workers typically got none of the job security or benefits, like PF, gratuity, or insurance, that direct government employees receive. This bill, moved by Finance Minister **Harpal Singh Cheema** on the last day of the Assembly's Monsoon Session, is Punjab's attempt to formally end that arrangement for eligible workers in essential public services.

stories.title: Supreme Court orders panel to verify why 24,000 Manipur violence-hit families still haven't received relief
stories.what_happened: On Monday, August 10, the Supreme Court asked its Gita Mittal-led committee to verify claims that roughly **24,000 families** affected by the 2023 Manipur ethnic violence have still not received the benefits due to them under government rehabilitation and welfare schemes. A bench of Chief Justice **Surya Kant** and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana heard submissions from senior advocate **Colin Gonsalves**, representing affected tribal communities, that many families remain without support more than two years after the violence began. The court also asked the Manipur and Assam governments to consider setting up **two special trial courts** to exclusively handle CBI and NIA cases arising from the violence. On the reconstruction front, funds have reached just over **4,000 of roughly 7,000** identified beneficiaries for rebuilding destroyed homes, while more than **12,000 houses** have been approved under the Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana-Gramin rural housing scheme.
key_points: The Supreme Court asked a panel led by **Justice Gita Mittal** to verify claims that **~24,000 families** haven't received promised rehabilitation benefits.
The court also asked Manipur and Assam to consider **two special trial courts** for CBI and NIA cases from the 2023 violence.
So far, only **~4,000 of 7,000** identified beneficiaries have received house-reconstruction funds.
More than **12,000 houses** have been approved under a federal rural housing scheme for affected families.
Chief Justice **Surya Kant** led the bench that heard submissions from senior advocate Colin Gonsalves on the tribals' behalf.

depth.background: Ethnic violence broke out in Manipur in May 2023 between the majority Meitei community and the Kuki-Zo tribal communities, after a court order reignited a long-running dispute over Scheduled Tribe status. More than 200 people have been killed and thousands displaced in the years since, with many still living in relief camps. The Supreme Court has kept the state's rehabilitation effort under close watch, appointing a committee of retired women high court judges — chaired by Justice Gita Mittal — to monitor relief and reconstruction. Two years on, this week's hearing shows how much of that promised rehabilitation remains undelivered.

stories.title: Supreme Court agrees to urgently hear Tamil Nadu's Cauvery water plea against Karnataka on August 13
stories.what_happened: The Supreme Court agreed to hear Tamil Nadu's plea on **August 13**, seeking directions to Karnataka for the immediate release of the state's share of Cauvery water. A bench comprising **Chief Justice Surya Kant** and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana took note of Tamil Nadu's submission that it was not getting its due share of water in a rain-deficient year. Tamil Nadu's government, led by Chief Minister Joseph Vijay, had approached the court on August 3 seeking implementation of a **July 30 CWMA decision** ordering Karnataka to release 3,500 cusecs of water daily from its Kabini and Krishna Raja Sagara reservoirs for 15 days. Tamil Nadu is seeking a total of **4.536 TMC** of water — calculated from that daily rate — delivered on or before August 12, a day ahead of the scheduled hearing.
key_points: The Supreme Court will hear Tamil Nadu's plea for **immediate Cauvery water release** from Karnataka on **August 13**.
A bench led by **Chief Justice Surya Kant** took up the case after Tamil Nadu said it wasn't getting its due share in a rain-deficient year.
Tamil Nadu wants Karnataka to release **3,500 cusecs of water daily for 15 days**, as ordered by the Cauvery Water Management Authority on July 30.
The state is seeking a total of **4.536 TMC** of water, delivered by **August 12** — a day before the court hearing.
Tamil Nadu's government, led by Chief Minister Joseph Vijay, moved the court on August 3 after Karnataka did not comply with the CWMA order.

depth.background: The Cauvery river dispute is one of India's oldest and most bitter inter-state water fights, pitting Tamil Nadu against Karnataka over sharing water from a river both states depend on for irrigation and drinking supply. A body called the **Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA)** was set up to enforce agreed water-sharing formulas and settle disputes between the states, but its orders are not always followed without a court push. Tensions escalate especially in years of weak monsoon rainfall, when there simply isn't enough water to satisfy both states' irrigation needs — 2026 has been one of those years.

stories.title: Taiwan deliberately slows mobile internet for 16 million people in a first-ever wartime-readiness test
stories.what_happened: On August 10, Taiwan's telecom regulators and the military ran a coordinated test that reduced mobile data speeds to roughly **1% of capacity** for an estimated **16 million residents** across Miaoli, Taichung, Changhua, Nantou, Yunlin, Chiayi county and Chiayi city, with the central-Taiwan window running from **2:30 to 3:00pm** local time as one of several staggered regional slots through the exercise. Phones still worked for calls, texts and emergency services, but everyday tasks that rely on fast data — mobile payments, ride-hailing, news apps, banking — slowed to a crawl or failed outright for the duration. The drill sits inside **Han Kuang 42**, Taiwan's largest yearly military exercise (Aug 5–14, ~20,000 active-duty and reserve troops), which this year for the first time formally combines the military wargame with civilian 'Urban Resilience' air-defence drills. China's state-run Global Times dismissed the exercise as a 'performance,' while Taiwanese officials framed it as necessary preparation for a scenario where an adversary disrupts communications ahead of, or during, a military move.
key_points: Taiwan cut 4G/5G speeds to about **1% of normal** across 14 cities and counties, in staggered 30-minute windows through the day.
The throttling is part of **Han Kuang 42**, Taiwan's largest annual military exercise, running **August 5–14** with ~20,000 personnel.
It is the **first time ever** civilian telecoms have been deliberately degraded to rehearse a wartime scenario.
Emergency numbers (110/119), voice calls, SMS and disaster alerts stay **fully operational** during the drill.
Defence Minister Wellington Koo called it a test of **'command-and-control backup capabilities under wartime-like conditions.'**

depth.background: Taiwan has run the **Han Kuang** exercise annually since **1984** to rehearse defending the island against a Chinese invasion or blockade, but this year is the first to fold in a full civilian 'Urban Resilience' track alongside the military drills. Beijing considers Taiwan part of its territory and has never renounced the use of force to bring it under control, and in recent years has increasingly used so-called **'gray-zone' tactics** — military pressure that stays just below the threshold of open war, like naval incursions, cyber probes and economic coercion — instead of outright attack. Planners in Taipei worry that in a real crisis China could try to sever or jam the island's communications before any shots are fired, which is exactly the scenario this drill tests.

stories.title: Trent Rockets Women can seal top spot as The Hundred's group stage wraps up against Southern Brave
stories.what_happened: Trent Rockets Women host Southern Brave at Trent Bridge, Nottingham, in their final group match of the 2026 season. Rockets go in top of the table on 24 points from seven matches (six wins, one loss), with Southern Brave just behind on 20 points from seven games (five wins, two losses). A win for Rockets today confirms them not just for the knockout stage — already secured — but for a direct place in the final, skipping the eliminator round altogether. The match follows a run of five straight wins for the Rockets, powered by Bates' economical spin and middle-order form from Sciver-Brunt and Mooney, who between them have carried the batting through the back half of the group stage.
key_points: Trent Rockets Women, already qualified for the knockouts, can **confirm a place in the final** with a win today.
They enter on a **five-match winning streak**, level-top of the table with **24 points from seven games**.
Southern Brave sit **second on 20 points**, so today's result at Trent Bridge decides the group's top seed.
Rockets' recent form has been driven by **Sam Bates' spin bowling** and big partnerships from Nat Sciver-Brunt and Beth Mooney.
The match caps the group stage of The Hundred Women's Competition 2026 before the knockouts begin.

depth.background: The Hundred is an English franchise cricket competition, running men's and women's tournaments side by side each August, with eight city-based teams playing a 100-ball-per-innings format. Trent Rockets Women have been the standout side of this year's women's competition, and had already all-but-secured a top-three finish and a knockout spot after a dominant chase against MI London — where **Nat Sciver-Brunt (67 not out)** and **Beth Mooney (54 not out)** put on the second-highest partnership in the competition's history, while spinner **Sam Bates** took 3 wickets for just 13 runs.

stories.title: Erik Roy's unbeaten 94 powers Jorhat Stallions to a 9-wicket rout of Tezpur Titans in the Assam Premier League
stories.what_happened: In the Assam Premier League's 19th match at the **ACA Stadium**, Tezpur Titans batted first and scored **160/6** in their 20 overs, with **Danish Ahmed** contributing an unbeaten 36 off just 15 balls late on. In reply, **Jorhat Stallions** chased the target down comfortably, finishing at **162/1 in 18.1 overs** — a **9-wicket win** with 11 balls to spare. Opener **Erik Roy** led the chase with an unbeaten **94**, and **Swarupam Purkayastha** finished things off with an unbeaten 34 off 20 balls.
key_points: **Jorhat Stallions** beat **Tezpur Titans** by **9 wickets** at the ACA Stadium in the inaugural Assam Premier League.
Opener **Erik Roy** smashed an unbeaten **94** to lead the chase.
Tezpur Titans posted **160/6**; Jorhat Stallions chased it down in **18.1 overs**, losing just one wicket.
**Swarupam Purkayastha** finished the match with an unbeaten **34 off 20 balls**.

depth.background: The **Assam Premier League** is a brand-new franchise T20 competition launched in August 2026 — the first of its kind for Assam — featuring eight teams including Jorhat Stallions and Tezpur Titans, part of a wider wave of state-level T20 leagues that have sprung up across India to build a domestic talent pipeline outside the IPL.

stories.title: Ukraine's drone commander warns Russia is building toward firing 200 ballistic missiles in a single strike
stories.what_happened: Ukraine's drone forces commander said Monday that Russia is working to expand its ballistic missile capacity to the point where it could fire roughly **200 missiles in a single combined attack** — nearly triple the scale of Russia's largest strikes to date this year, which have topped out around 40-93 missiles alongside drone swarms. The commander framed this as the core argument for two things Ukraine has pushed for months: strikes on the **Russian factories that build these missiles**, rather than relying solely on shooting them down after launch, and cutting off **Crimea's role as a military staging base** that supports strikes on Ukrainian territory. The statement did not describe an attack that has already happened — it is a warning about where Russia's capacity is heading, based on Ukrainian military assessments.
key_points: Ukraine's **drone forces commander** says Russia is working to **nearly triple** its ballistic missile firepower per strike.
The goal, per the warning: a single attack of roughly **200 ballistic missiles** at once, far above Russia's largest strikes so far this year.
The claim is being used to argue for hitting **Russian missile factories directly**, not just intercepting missiles after launch.
It also ties into pressure to choke off **Crimea's use as a military staging base** for Russian strikes.
No attack of this stated scale has happened yet — this is a **warning about capacity**, not a completed strike.

depth.background: Russia has escalated the scale of its missile-and-drone strikes on Ukraine repeatedly through 2026, with attacks combining dozens of ballistic missiles and over a hundred drones in a single night targeting power grids and cities. Ukraine's air defense depends on intercepting as many of these as possible, but has repeatedly warned its interceptor stocks are strained — a near-total interceptor shortage was flagged just this month around fighting near Kharkiv. Ukrainian officials increasingly argue that intercepting missiles is a losing game if Russia can keep building more of them, and have pushed instead for strikes on the **factories and bases** that produce and launch them, including on the Crimean peninsula, which Russia annexed in 2014 and uses as a logistics and airbase hub for strikes on southern and eastern Ukraine.

stories.title: A 7.4-magnitude earthquake kills at least 132 people in western Colombia, its deadliest in decades
stories.what_happened: A **magnitude-7.4 earthquake** struck western Colombia at 7:34am local time on Monday, August 10, with its epicenter near San José del Palmar in Chocó province at a depth of 79km. The shaking was felt roughly 250 miles away in the capital, Bogotá, and triggered building collapses across several regions. Authorities have confirmed **132 deaths and 570 injuries** so far, with the worst-hit areas being Risaralda (40 dead, centered on the city of Pereira) and Valle del Cauca (27 dead, centered on Cali, where residents were trapped in at least 19 collapsed buildings). More than 1,600 buildings were damaged, and video showed part of Manizales' Metropolitan Cathedral Basilica crumbling. Regional airports including Pereira, Manizales, Quibdó, Armenia, Cartago and Buenaventura suspended flights to check for structural damage. President Abelardo De La Espriella declared a national disaster to speed the release of emergency funds and rescue teams.
key_points: A **7.4-magnitude earthquake** struck Colombia's Chocó region at **7:34am local time** Monday, epicenter near San José del Palmar.
At least **132 people are confirmed dead** and **570 injured**, with the toll expected to rise as rescuers reach rural areas.
More than **1,600 buildings** were damaged, and buildings collapsed in **Cali**, a city of 2 million people.
Newly inaugurated president **Abelardo De La Espriella** declared a **national disaster** to mobilize emergency response.
The quake struck **79km underground** — a depth that meant no tsunami formed despite the size of the shock.

depth.background: Colombia sits on one of the world's most seismically active zones, part of the Pacific **'Ring of Fire'** where the Nazca oceanic plate slides beneath the South American plate. Large, damaging quakes are a recurring risk here — a 1999 quake near Armenia killed over 1,000 people — and Colombia's Geological Service says this is the **strongest to hit the country in the 21st century**. The hardest-hit province, Chocó, is one of Colombia's poorest and most rural regions, with many areas reachable only by boat or small plane, which is slowing rescue efforts. At least 21 aftershocks have followed the main quake, complicating search-and-rescue in already-damaged buildings.

stories.title: East Delhi Riders chase down 183 to beat West Delhi Lions by 5 wickets in the Delhi Premier League
stories.what_happened: In Match 20 of the 2026 Delhi Premier League at **Arun Jaitley Stadium**, West Delhi Lions batted first and posted **182/9** in their 20 overs. In reply, **East Delhi Riders** chased the target down successfully, finishing at **183/5 in 19 overs** to win by **5 wickets** with an over in hand.
key_points: **East Delhi Riders** chased down **183** in 19 overs to beat **West Delhi Lions** by **5 wickets** at Arun Jaitley Stadium.
West Delhi Lions had posted **182/9** batting first in their 20 overs.
The result was Match 20 of the **2026 Delhi Premier League (DPL)**, Delhi's franchise T20 tournament.
It was a tight run-chase, decided with **one over to spare**.

depth.background: The **Delhi Premier League** is Delhi's own city-level T20 franchise competition, similar in format to the IPL but featuring local and domestic players across teams representing different parts of the capital, including **West Delhi Lions** and **East Delhi Riders**. These domestic T20 leagues have grown across Indian states in recent years as a platform for talent below IPL level to get competitive franchise cricket.

stories.title: Nepal names Sandeep Lamichhane its new ODI captain, replacing Rohit Paudel ahead of the ACC Premier Cup
stories.what_happened: The Cricket Association of Nepal named **Sandeep Lamichhane** as the team's new ODI captain, taking over from Rohit Paudel, who had led the side successfully including winning 11 of 12 matches in the ICC Cricket World Cup League 2. It marks Lamichhane's second stint in charge, after his first was cut short in 2022 when CAN suspended him following an arrest warrant. His first assignment as captain will be the **ACC Men's Premier Cup**, an Asian regional tournament being held in Malaysia from August 30 to September 12.
key_points: Leg-spinner **Sandeep Lamichhane**, who has taken 154 wickets in 77 ODIs, becomes Nepal's ODI captain again.
He replaces **Rohit Paudel**, under whom Nepal won 11 of 12 ODIs in the ICC Cricket World Cup League 2.
It's Lamichhane's **second stint** as captain — his first ended in 2022 when he was suspended after an arrest warrant.
The change comes ahead of the **ACC Men's Premier Cup**, running in Malaysia from **August 30 to September 12**.
At 26, Lamichhane is one of Nepal's most recognizable cricketers and a T20 franchise regular worldwide.

depth.background: Nepal has become one of the more competitive Associate cricket nations over the past several years, regularly punching above its weight in qualifying tournaments. Sandeep Lamichhane, a leg-spin bowler who has played in T20 leagues around the world, previously captained Nepal before being suspended by the Cricket Association of Nepal (CAN) in 2022 after an arrest warrant was issued against him; Rohit Paudel then took over and led the side successfully, including an 11-from-12 ODI winning run in the ICC Cricket World Cup League 2, a tournament that feeds into qualification for the 50-over World Cup.

stories.title: F1 boss Domenicali says he's held 'constructive' talks with Verstappen about staying beyond 2026
stories.what_happened: Formula 1's commercial boss Stefano Domenicali revealed he has held direct conversations with Verstappen about his future in the sport, tying the discussion to F1's upcoming 2027 power-unit regulation changes. Domenicali said 'I think that Max is in a situation where he loves Formula 1, he loves the future. We are discussing together his future, and the regulations for the future,' adding 'My opinion is that Max will stay with us. And I really hope so.' The comments come as Red Bull has already offered Verstappen a new contract that removes his exit clause and includes a significant pay increase, an offer he has not yet accepted. Domenicali's remarks are the clearest public signal yet from F1's leadership that they are actively working to keep Verstappen in the sport past this season.
key_points: F1 CEO **Stefano Domenicali** confirmed direct talks with Max Verstappen about his F1 future.
Domenicali said: **'My opinion is that Max will stay with us. And I really hope so.'**
The talks are tied to **2027 power-unit regulation changes** the sport is finalising.
Verstappen holds an **exit clause** in his Red Bull contract that is reportedly now 'firmly in play'.
Red Bull has separately offered him a new deal with **no exit clause and a large raise**, which he hasn't accepted.

depth.background: Max Verstappen, F1's reigning multi-time champion, has an **exit clause** in his Red Bull contract — a provision letting him leave the team early under specified conditions — that has fuelled a summer of speculation about whether he'll stay at Red Bull, move to a rival team, or even step away from F1 altogether. His future is one of the biggest storylines of this year's driver market ('silly season'), since a Verstappen departure from Red Bull would set off a chain reaction across multiple teams' lineups.

stories.title: Ukrainian drones hit one of Russia's biggest oil refineries 1,200km inside Tatarstan, killing at least 12
stories.what_happened: Ukraine's General Staff confirmed on Monday that its forces struck the **Taneco oil refinery** in Nizhnekamsk, Tatarstan, one of Russia's most advanced facilities with an annual processing capacity of **over 16 million tonnes**. A fire broke out at the plant after the strike. Tatarstan's regional head, Rustam Minnikhanov, said the attack killed **at least 12 people**, including a child, and injured 39 more. Russia's defence ministry claimed its air defenses intercepted **456 Ukrainian drones** across the country overnight, while separately, explosions and a drone attack knocked out power to parts of **Simferopol**, the capital of Russian-occupied Crimea. Fires were also reported in Donetsk Oblast. The strike came a day after Ukraine hit two other Russian refineries, Ilsky and Syzran.
key_points: Ukraine's military confirmed a strike on the **Taneco refinery** in Nizhnekamsk, Tatarstan — one of Russia's largest, processing **over 16 million tonnes of oil a year**.
Tatarstan's regional government says the drone attack killed **at least 12 people** and injured 39.
The refinery sits roughly **1,200 km from the Ukrainian border**, deep inside Russia's Volga heartland, far beyond the usual front-line target zone.
Russia claims it intercepted **456 drones** nationwide overnight; Crimea's capital Simferopol also lost power in a related strike.
This is part of a **deliberate campaign** against Russia's oil-refining capacity, not just border-region targets.

depth.background: For much of 2026, Ukraine has shifted from trying to intercept every incoming Russian missile and drone — a losing numbers game — toward hitting the **factories and refineries that fuel and fund Russia's war**. Just yesterday, Ukrainian strikes set two refineries, Ilsky and Syzran, ablaze; today's hit on Taneco in Tatarstan pushes that campaign further from the border than almost any previous strike. **Tatarstan** is a Volga-region republic more than 1,000km from Ukraine, a part of Russia that has rarely felt the war directly until this year. Ukraine's logic: refined fuel, not crude oil, is what keeps tanks moving and jets flying, so refineries are higher-value targets than oilfields.

thread.previously: Yesterday's brief covered Ukraine setting Russia's Ilsky and Syzran refineries ablaze in strikes on Russia's oil infrastructure and defence industry.
thread.changed: Today's strike hit the Taneco refinery in Tatarstan — about 1,200km inside Russia, far deeper than previous targets — killing at least 12 people, the deadliest and most distant refinery strike in this campaign so far.
