stories.title: Israeli forces fire on Palestinians in Khan Younis as Gaza's Hamas-disarmament standoff drags on
stories.what_happened: On Saturday, August 8, Israeli forces fired on a gathering of Palestinians north of Khan Younis in southern Gaza, injuring three people, while separately carrying out demolition operations south of the city since Saturday morning. The incident is one of many smaller flare-ups Palestinian officials say have continued despite the ceasefire, with more than **1,230 Palestinians killed and over 4,000 injured** since October 2025 by their count. The United Nations has said roughly **300 children have been killed in 300 days** of the supposed ceasefire. Behind the daily violence sits a bigger standoff: on August 4, the Board of Peace's director Nickolay Mladenov met Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu and reaffirmed that Israel will not withdraw before Hamas's disarmament is confirmed, even as Israeli politicians voice unease with parts of Trump's own plan.
key_points: Israeli troops opened fire on Palestinians gathered north of **Khan Younis** on Saturday, injuring **3 people**.
The incident came alongside ongoing **demolition operations** by Israeli forces south of the city.
It's the latest of what Palestinian officials call **thousands of ceasefire violations** since October 2025.
The core dispute: Hamas must disarm within **90 days** under a US-brokered plan before Israel will fully withdraw.
The **Board of Peace**, the US-led body overseeing the deal, says withdrawal will not happen before disarmament is verified.

depth.background: An October 2025 ceasefire ended the most intense phase of the Gaza war, but fighting never fully stopped. In late July 2026, President Trump announced a **Hamas disarmament plan**: the group has 90 days to hand over heavy weapons and 8 months to allow destruction of its tunnel network, after which Israeli forces are supposed to withdraw completely. Israel's government, however, says it will not pull troops out until Hamas is verifiably disarmed, and accuses the group of planning to rebuild its military capability rather than genuinely demilitarising. Hamas, in turn, says it will only disarm if the process leads toward an eventual Palestinian state — a demand Israel's current government rejects outright.

stories.title: Zelensky makes his first-ever visit to Serbia, meeting a Russia-friendly Vučić
stories.what_happened: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky traveled to Belgrade for an official visit on **August 8**, his first to Serbia since taking office. He is meeting Serbian President **Aleksandar Vučić** and Prime Minister Đuro Macut to discuss deepening economic ties, energy cooperation, and both countries' paths toward **European Union membership**. Vučić, asked whether the visit signals a shift in Serbia's stance on Russia, said Belgrade's sanctions policy was set **nearly five years ago** and will not change "for the foreseeable future." The visit comes as Zelensky continues a broader diplomatic push across Europe to keep allies engaged in Ukraine's defense and reconstruction planning.
key_points: Volodymyr Zelensky arrived in Belgrade on **his first visit to Serbia** since Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine.
Serbia is one of the few European countries that has **refused to join Western sanctions on Russia**.
The two leaders are expected to discuss **EU integration, energy cooperation, and expanding trade ties**.
Serbian President **Aleksandar Vučić** said Serbia's sanctions policy, set nearly **five years ago**, will not change.

depth.background: Serbia has walked a careful line since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine began in **February 2022**: it has condemned the invasion at the UN but refused to impose sanctions on Moscow, partly because of deep historic, religious and economic ties to Russia. Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić has cultivated relationships with both the West (Serbia is an EU candidate country) and Russia, buying time rather than picking a side. Zelensky, by contrast, has spent his presidency touring allied capitals to shore up military and financial support for Ukraine's defense. This trip is his **first as president to Belgrade**, a notable gesture toward a government that has stayed publicly neutral.

stories.title: Pakistan's Test squad lands in England as Bethell is ruled out and England recall Pope and Carse
stories.what_happened: Pakistan's Test squad, captained by Babar Azam, landed in England on Saturday morning to begin preparations for a three-match series forming part of the ICC World Test Championship 2025-27 cycle. The team trains from Monday at the County Ground in Beckenham before a four-day practice match against a Select XI from **August 12-15**. Separately, England named its 16-man squad for the series: **Jacob Bethell will miss the entirety** of the series, while **Ollie Pope and Brydon Carse have been recalled** for the first time since the Ashes. The first Test starts **August 19 at Headingley in Leeds**, running to August 23, followed by the second Test at **Lord's from August 27-31**.
key_points: **Pakistan's Test squad**, led by Babar Azam, arrived in England on Saturday for a **3-match series**
England left-hander **Jacob Bethell will miss the entire series**, while Ollie Pope and Brydon Carse are recalled
The series opens **August 19 at Headingley**, followed by Lord's (Aug 27) in the WTC 2025-27 cycle
Joe Root leads England in Tests for the first time at home since **Ben Stokes' retirement** from international cricket
Pakistan play a four-day warm-up match against a Select XI from **August 12-15** before the series starts

depth.background: Ben Stokes shocked the cricket world by announcing his retirement from international cricket mid-Test in June 2026, ending a 15-year England career and 4-year Test captaincy. Joe Root has since taken over as England's Test captain. Pakistan's tour of England is part of the **ICC World Test Championship 2025-27 cycle**, the league table that decides which two teams reach the WTC final; results in individual series feed directly into a team's overall points percentage.

stories.title: ISRO launches its heaviest-ever satellite, carrying a US direct-to-mobile spacecraft
stories.what_happened: ISRO successfully launched the BlueBird Block-2 satellite aboard its LVM3-M6 rocket from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota, Andhra Pradesh, at 8:55 AM IST today. After a roughly 15-minute flight, the satellite separated cleanly and was placed into its planned orbit. ISRO Chairman V. Narayanan called it the heaviest satellite ever lifted off Indian soil by an Indian launch vehicle. BlueBird Block-2 will join AST SpaceMobile's growing constellation of satellites designed to provide direct-to-mobile broadband connectivity as part of a global low-Earth-orbit (LEO) network.
key_points: ISRO's **LVM3-M6** rocket lifted off from Sriharikota at **8:55 AM IST** today, carrying the **BlueBird Block-2** satellite.
It is the **heaviest satellite ever launched from Indian soil** on an Indian rocket, per ISRO chairman **V. Narayanan**.
BlueBird Block-2 belongs to **AST SpaceMobile**, a US company building satellites that connect ordinary smartphones directly, with no special hardware.
The spacecraft separated from the rocket about **15 minutes** after liftoff and was placed into its intended orbit.
It's part of a growing trend of India launching heavy **commercial payloads** for foreign satellite operators.

depth.background: ISRO's LVM3 (formerly GSLV Mk III) is India's most powerful operational rocket, originally built to launch India's own heavy communication satellites and the Chandrayaan Moon missions. In recent years ISRO's commercial arm has increasingly sold launch capacity to foreign companies needing to loft heavy satellites cheaply and reliably. AST SpaceMobile is a US company racing Elon Musk's Starlink and others to build 'direct-to-cell' satellite networks — space-based cell towers that let unmodified smartphones send texts and calls without a local mobile signal.

stories.title: R. Vinay Kumar set to become Karnataka's head coach for the new domestic season
stories.what_happened: Karnataka is set to appoint former India fast bowler R. Vinay Kumar as head coach for the 2026-27 domestic season, according to PTI, with the appointment expected to be formally finalised soon. He replaces outgoing coach Yere Goud, who is moving into a batting-coach role at the BCCI's Centre of Excellence. The coaching reshuffle also brings in Vinay's former Karnataka teammate Deepak Chougule as fielding coach, while current bowling coach Mansur Ali Khan is expected to continue in his role. The change comes as Karnataka transitions to a new captain, Devdutt Padikkal, with several younger players trying to establish themselves in the side.
key_points: Former India pacer **R. Vinay Kumar** is set to take over as **Karnataka's head coach** for the **2026-27 domestic season**.
He replaces **Yere Goud**, who is moving to the BCCI's Centre of Excellence as a batting coach.
Vinay takes charge as Karnataka rebuilds under new captain **Devdutt Padikkal**.
Former teammate **Deepak Chougule** is set to join as fielding coach; current bowling coach **Mansur Ali Khan** is likely to stay on.
Vinay previously worked as a TV commentator, an IPL talent scout for Mumbai Indians, and bowling coach of MI Emirates in the ILT20.

depth.background: Karnataka is one of Indian domestic cricket's most successful state teams, having produced players like Rahul Dravid, Anil Kumble and Javagal Srinath. R. Vinay Kumar was a right-arm pace bowler who played for India and had a long, successful career for Karnataka, including as captain, before retiring from playing in 2021. Domestic coaching appointments like this set the tone for a state team's young talent pipeline heading into the Ranji Trophy and other first-class competitions.

stories.title: Bus plunges 100 feet into a Himachal Pradesh gorge, killing at least 7
stories.what_happened: The bus was travelling from Bairagarh to Chamba town on Saturday morning when it skidded off the road near the Chalunj bend, overturned, and fell roughly 100 feet onto the road below. Local residents began rescue efforts before police and administrative teams arrived to take over. At least **7 people were killed** — including the bus driver and conductor — and **11 injured** people were taken to a hospital in nearby Tissa town. Officials have not yet determined the exact cause, and an investigation into the circumstances of the crash is underway.
key_points: A private passenger bus rolled off a hill road on the **Bairagarh–Chamba route** in Himachal Pradesh's Chamba district on Saturday morning.
It fell around **100 feet (roughly 30 metres)** into a gorge near the Chalunj bend after skidding off the road.
At least **7 people died**, including the driver and conductor, and **11 more were injured**.
Around **20–25 passengers**, mostly locals travelling to Chamba town, were on board at the time.

depth.background: Chamba is a remote, mountainous district in northern Himachal Pradesh where narrow, unpaved or poorly maintained roads wind along steep gorges — a common and recurring hazard across the Himalayan states. Overloaded private buses are the main form of public transport for people in these hill towns, since road infrastructure and traffic policing are thin. Fatal bus-into-gorge accidents are tragically frequent in Himachal Pradesh and neighbouring Uttarakhand, often blamed on a mix of bad roads, monsoon-weakened surfaces, and vehicle overcrowding.

stories.title: Bottas shuts down Cadillac exit rumors as Herta links swirl, confirms 2026 car development is winding down
stories.what_happened: Bottas has publicly pushed back on speculation that Cadillac could drop him for its second F1 season, saying: **'I know what my contract says, and the team supports me 100 percent. I will definitely be here next year as well.'** The rumors were fueled by Cadillac being the **only team on the entire grid without a single championship point** at the summer break, while teammate Sergio Pérez has clearly outperformed him — and by reports that **Colton Herta**, an IndyCar star with ties to Cadillac's junior program, could be lined up as a replacement. Bottas said he expects the car to improve materially, adding **'in two months our car will be much faster.'** In a related interview, he also confirmed Cadillac will soon stop developing its 2026 car entirely to redirect resources toward 2027: **'there is a point that we need to shift our focus 100 per cent for next year, which is coming soon.'**
key_points: Valtteri Bottas says his **Cadillac contract is secure** for 2027 despite growing speculation he could be dropped.
Cadillac is F1's newest team and the **only one on the grid without a single point** at the summer break.
IndyCar star **Colton Herta**, backed by Cadillac's junior program, has been floated as a possible 2027 replacement.
Bottas says Cadillac will soon **stop developing its 2026 car** to focus fully on next year's challenger.
Teammate **Sergio Pérez** has comfortably outscored Bottas so far, fueling the speculation.

depth.background: **Cadillac**, General Motors' brand, joined F1 as its **11th team for 2026** — the first new constructor since Haas in 2016. It signed two experienced veterans, **Sergio Pérez** (a six-time race winner, formerly of Red Bull) and **Valtteri Bottas** (ex-Mercedes and Williams, 10 career wins), rather than rookies, specifically to speed up its learning curve as a brand-new team. Scoring **zero points** through the first half of the season is a rough start for a team that talked up big ambitions when it launched.

stories.title: Lewis Hamilton backed for a genuine 2026 title fight as Ferrari doubles down
stories.what_happened: In an interview published today, 1972 and 1974 world champion Emerson Fittipaldi said he'd like to see Hamilton fight seriously for the title, calling it 'extremely good' for the sport if he could take the fight to Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli. After 11 grands prix, Hamilton has a win and four further podium finishes, sitting second in the drivers' standings roughly 50 points behind Antonelli, who Fittipaldi and others note is driving the season's dominant car. Ferrari intends to keep its aggressive upgrade pace through the second half of the year, with a further engine update expected at Monza in September, while Mercedes' Antonelli and George Russell are both set to face engine-component grid penalties later in the season — a potential opportunity for Hamilton to close the points gap.
key_points: Two-time champion **Emerson Fittipaldi** says he believes Lewis Hamilton can mount a serious 2026 title challenge.
Hamilton sits **second in the championship**, roughly **50 points** behind leader Kimi Antonelli, with a win and four podiums from 11 races.
It's Hamilton's first genuine title fight since **2021** — his debut season at Ferrari after leaving Mercedes.
Ferrari plans to keep pushing aggressive car upgrades, with a new engine expected at **Monza**.
Mercedes rivals **Antonelli and George Russell** are set to take engine-related grid penalties later this season, a potential opening for Hamilton.

depth.background: Lewis Hamilton, a seven-time world champion, left Mercedes for Ferrari ahead of the 2025 season in one of F1's biggest-ever driver moves, but his first year and a half at Maranello were rocky by his own standards. The 2026 rules reset — new engines and cars for everyone — reshuffled competitiveness across the grid, and Ferrari has emerged as one of the fastest-developing teams, aided by team-mate Charles Leclerc's pace and an unusually aggressive stream of upgrades.

stories.title: Private bus plunges off a mountain road in Himachal Pradesh's Chamba district, killing 7
stories.what_happened: A private bus travelling from **Bairagarh towards Chamba** went off the road near a curve called **Chalunj Mor** early on Saturday morning, around **7:15 am**, and fell onto another road below. **Seven people were killed** and **11 others injured** in the crash. Six of the injured were referred to Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru Government Medical College and Hospital in Chamba for further treatment. Police said rescue teams were dispatched immediately after the accident was reported, and relief and rescue operations were launched at the site. The stretch of road involved — the Tissa-Bairagarh route — is a narrow, 27-kilometre mountain road through the remote Churah Valley known for its sharp bends and unguarded drops.
key_points: A private bus went off the **Bairagarh-Chamba road** and fell onto a lower road near **Chalunj Mor**.
At least **7 people were killed** and **11 injured** in the crash, early Saturday morning.
The accident happened around **7:15 am** on a narrow, steep mountain route in the remote **Churah Valley**.
Six of the injured were referred to **Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru Government Medical College**, Chamba, for treatment.
Police and rescue teams reached the site quickly and launched relief operations.

depth.background: Himachal Pradesh's hill roads — narrow, steep, and often poorly barricaded — see frequent bus and vehicle accidents, especially during the monsoon when rain weakens road edges and visibility drops. The **Tissa-Bairagarh road** through the Churah Valley is one of these treacherous mountain routes, a 27-kilometre stretch with sharp curves and steep drop-offs that connects remote villages to the district headquarters at Chamba. Fatal bus accidents in the state are unfortunately common enough that they recur several times a year, often blamed on a mix of poor road maintenance, aging vehicles, and driver error on hairpin bends.

stories.title: Ukraine's defensive line collapses near Orekhovo as Russian troops seize 50+ sq km in a day
stories.what_happened: Ukrainian and Russian military bloggers, along with the pro-Russian outlet Pravda EN, reported on the morning of **August 8** that Ukraine's western flank of defence around Orekhovo had collapsed, with Russian units advancing roughly 50–55 square kilometres in 24 hours — an unusually fast rate for this war. Russian forces are pushing from three directions simultaneously while trying to cut Ukrainian supply lines into the town. Ukraine's General Staff separately reported **192 combat engagements** as of 10pm on August 7, with the heaviest fighting around Pokrovsk further north, and said Russia struck with missiles, glide bombs and drones. If the western supply road into Orekhovo is severed to match the already-cut eastern one, Ukrainian units in the town could be surrounded. Kyiv's own casualty claims against Russia (1,190 troops, 1,751 drones in the same period) are the kind of daily figures both sides publish and that outside analysts treat with caution.
key_points: Russian forces overran roughly **50–55 square kilometres** west of Orekhovo (Orikhiv) in about 24 hours.
Ukraine's General Staff logged **192 combat engagements** in a single day, with the **Pokrovsk direction** the most intense.
The **eastern supply route** into Orekhovo was already cut; the new push threatens the **western route too**.
If both roads are severed, Ukrainian troops holding the town risk **full encirclement**.
Kyiv reports Russia lost **1,190+ troops and 1,751 drones** in the same 24 hours — a figure that cannot be independently verified.

depth.background: Orekhovo (Orikhiv in Ukrainian) is a small city in **Zaporizhzhia region** that has sat just behind the front line for most of the war, acting as a logistics hub for Ukrainian forces defending the wider Zaporizhzhia sector. Russia has spent months grinding forward here in small, costly advances rather than in one dramatic breakthrough. Military analysts, including the US-based **Institute for the Study of War's Critical Threats project**, have repeatedly cautioned that Russian state media exaggerates the pace of these advances as part of a deliberate information campaign, even though the underlying territorial gains are real.

stories.title: Rashid Khan takes 6/34 as Afghanistan thrash Ireland by 92 runs to lead their ODI series 1-0
stories.what_happened: Afghanistan beat Ireland by **92 runs** in the second ODI of their five-match series at Bready Cricket Club in Northern Ireland, in a match reduced to **47 overs a side** by rain. Batting first, Afghanistan posted **299/8**, with **Ibrahim Zadran** top-scoring on **84** and sharing a **116-run second-wicket partnership** with Sediqullah Atal. In reply, Ireland looked competitive early but collapsed dramatically, losing **7 wickets for just 63 runs** to be bowled out for **207**. **Cade Carmichael** top-scored for Ireland with **62**, while captain **Andy Balbirnie** and **Harry Tector** both fell caught behind to Rashid Khan in successive overs. Rashid finished with figures of **6 wickets for 34 runs** — his third career ODI five-plus-wicket haul — taking four of the last seven Irish wickets to fall. The win puts Afghanistan **1-0 up** in the five-match series after the opening ODI was washed out without a result.
key_points: Afghanistan beat Ireland by **92 runs** in the 2nd ODI at Bready, Northern Ireland, in a match reduced to **47 overs a side**.
**Ibrahim Zadran** top-scored with **84**, anchoring a **116-run stand** with Sediqullah Atal as Afghanistan posted **299/8**.
Ireland collapsed from a competitive position to **207 all out**, losing **7 wickets for just 63 runs**.
Captain **Rashid Khan** took **6/34** — his third career ODI five-plus-wicket haul, grabbing 4 of Ireland's last 7 wickets.
Afghanistan lead the **five-match series 1-0** after the first ODI was washed out by rain.

depth.background: **Rashid Khan** is Afghanistan's captain and one of the world's best leg-spin bowlers. Afghanistan's cricket team has risen fast over the past decade — they played their **first Test match in 2018** — and regularly beats established cricketing nations despite the country's relatively small playing base. **Ireland**, also a relatively new full member of world cricket, is in the middle of a rebuilding phase, and this series has been described by both sides as the start of a **new era** for each team.

stories.title: Verstappen gets a blunt 'reality check' on his 2026 title chances amid Red Bull frustration
stories.what_happened: Speaking to media on August 8, former F1 driver **Stefan Johansson** told Max Verstappen the plain "reality" of the sport: no driver has ever won a world title without having the best car underneath them, a pointed comment amid Verstappen's frustration with Red Bull's underperforming 2026 car. Verstappen has gone **11 races without a win** this season, collecting four podiums and 109 championship points, well off the pace of Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli, who leads the standings. Red Bull's first season building its own power unit has brought both engine and rear-wing reliability failures, adding to Verstappen's visible frustration through the year. He remains contracted to Red Bull until 2028, but a contractual exit clause has now activated, meaning he could leave for a rival team as early as 2027 if he decides Red Bull's power-unit project isn't converging fast enough.
key_points: Former F1 driver **Stefan Johansson** told Verstappen that **no champion has ever won without the best car**.
Verstappen is **winless through 11 races** in 2026, with 4 podiums and **109 points**.
Red Bull became an **F1 power-unit manufacturer for the first time ever** this year, and reliability has suffered.
Verstappen has suffered both **power-unit and rear-wing failures** this season.
He's contracted to Red Bull through 2028, but an **exit clause is now active**, letting him leave for 2027.

depth.background: Red Bull has dominated much of F1's recent history with Verstappen winning four straight drivers' titles, but 2026 brought sweeping new technical and power-unit regulations across the sport. For the first time, Red Bull chose to build its own engine in-house (via Red Bull Powertrains, working with Ford) rather than buy one from Honda, a major strategic gamble that has come with early reliability growing pains. Verstappen has an exit clause in his contract that has now activated, giving him the option to leave the team he has raced for since 2016 if he chooses to for the 2027 season.

stories.title: Kashmir's Counter Intelligence wing raids Anantnag, Shopian and Baramulla in an online terror-recruitment case
stories.what_happened: On Saturday, CIK teams conducted simultaneous search operations across **Anantnag, Shopian and Baramulla** districts. In Anantnag's Hiller Shahabad locality, a team led by a Deputy Superintendent of Police seized **two digital devices** from a residential house. The operation is tied to an existing FIR registered under Sections 153A (promoting enmity between groups) and 505 (statements conducive to public mischief) of the Indian Penal Code, alongside Sections 13 and 18 of the **Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA)** — India's principal anti-terror law. Authorities say the case involves the alleged misuse of online platforms to glorify terrorism and influence people to join terrorist organisations; the seized devices will undergo forensic analysis.
key_points: **Counter Intelligence Kashmir (CIK)** ran simultaneous search operations across **three districts** — Anantnag, Shopian and Baramulla — on Saturday.
At a house in Anantnag's Hiller Shahabad area, a CIK team seized **two digital devices** for forensic examination.
The case is registered under **UAPA** (India's anti-terror law) and IPC sections covering promoting enmity and spreading false statements.
It concerns the alleged **online glorification of terrorism** and using platforms to recruit or influence people toward terrorist organisations.
The raids follow a wider valley-wide crackdown launched after a **fatal terror attack on police** in Anantnag in July, which saw roughly **1,000 people detained** for questioning.

depth.background: Jammu and Kashmir has seen a sustained security crackdown since a terror attack killed a policeman in Anantnag district in late July 2026, triggering a valley-wide operation that has already detained around a thousand people across multiple districts. **CIK**, Kashmir's specialized counter-intelligence unit, investigates cases involving online radicalisation and terror financing/recruitment networks, working alongside broader Jammu and Kashmir Police counter-terror operations.

stories.title: Iranian missile hits a UAE-flagged tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, escalating the Gulf shipping crisis
stories.what_happened: Early Saturday, the United Arab Emirates said an Iranian missile struck a vessel affiliated with **ADNOC**, the state-owned Abu Dhabi National Oil Company, while it was transiting the Strait of Hormuz. ADNOC confirmed the strike in a statement and said there were **no casualties**, but noted this is part of a pattern: **more than a dozen** of its vessels have now been hit by missiles or drones while passing through the strait since the war began. The UAE formally condemned the attack. The incident comes even as Iran claims a shipping-management deal with Oman is in its final drafting stages — a deal the US reportedly still won't accept on Iran's proposed terms.
key_points: A vessel owned by Abu Dhabi's state oil giant **ADNOC** was struck by an Iranian missile early Saturday while transiting the Strait of Hormuz.
**ADNOC says there were no casualties**, but this is now one of **over a dozen** of its ships attacked since the US-Israel war on Iran began in **February 2026**.
Iran has effectively **blockaded the strait** and is demanding ships pay a toll to pass — something the **US flatly rejects**.
The attack lands even as Iran and Oman claim to have a **draft deal** on managing the strait, exposing how fragile that arrangement really is.
About **one-fifth of global oil** normally flows through this single 33km-wide waterway.

depth.background: The Strait of Hormuz is the narrow channel between Iran and Oman that virtually all Gulf oil exports — from Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Kuwait, Iraq and Iran itself — must pass through to reach world markets. Since the **US and Israel struck Iran in February 2026**, killing the previous Supreme Leader, Iran has retaliated by harassing and periodically closing the strait to pressure Washington and its Gulf allies. Iran's parliament has floated a bill to charge tolls on all shipping except US and Israeli vessels, which it wants banned outright. **Oman has been mediating** a deal to formalize passage rules, but Washington has so far refused Iran's asking price.

stories.title: Honda's upgraded engine for Aston Martin could add up to 50 extra horsepower when it debuts at the Dutch Grand Prix
stories.what_happened: Honda confirmed it has completed the 'last phase' of a major upgrade to the power unit it supplies Aston Martin, aimed primarily at the internal combustion engine and at reducing internal friction to free up extra performance. Reports across the paddock estimate the gain at somewhere between **30 horsepower** (Honda's own conservative framing) and **50-plus horsepower** (per paddock rumors), which would be a substantial mid-season jump in a sport where lap times are often decided by fractions of a second. The upgraded unit was fitted to Aston Martin's car for a filming day following the Hungarian Grand Prix in late July as an early, low-pressure shakedown, ahead of its real competitive debut at the **Dutch Grand Prix**, the first race back from F1's August summer break.
key_points: Honda has finished developing a **B-spec power unit upgrade** for Aston Martin, focused on the internal combustion engine and reduced friction.
Paddock estimates put the gain at **30 to 50+ horsepower** — a significant jump mid-season.
The new engine was quietly tested in Aston Martin's car during a **post-Hungarian GP filming day**, before its real competitive debut.
It's set to race for the first time at the **Dutch Grand Prix** after F1's August summer shutdown.
Honda says the upgrade also targets **better reliability**, not just raw power.

depth.background: In Formula 1, teams don't build their own engines from scratch every year — most buy 'power units' from manufacturers like Honda, Mercedes, or Ferrari, and mid-season upgrades to those engines can meaningfully shift the competitive order without any change to the car's aerodynamics. **Aston Martin** switched to Honda power for the 2026 season as part of a broader realignment of engine partnerships. Since F1 introduced new engine regulations for 2026, teams have been racing to find performance gains within a tightly constrained rulebook, making even a modest horsepower increase like this one a big deal relative to rivals.

stories.title: F1's revenue crashed 38% last quarter — but it's because of fewer races, not falling popularity
stories.what_happened: Liberty Media's Q2 2026 report showed F1 revenue of **$764 million**, a **38% drop** from $1.22 billion in Q2 2025. Operating income collapsed from $293 million to **$73 million**, and adjusted operating income before depreciation (OIBDA) fell **61%** to $139 million from $361 million. The core reason: F1 held only **five Grands Prix** in the quarter, compared to nine the year before, after Middle East tensions forced several races to be postponed. Despite the revenue hit, **total viewing hours rose 13%** year-on-year, and Liberty pointed to newly signed long-term commercial deals — extending the **Las Vegas Grand Prix contract to 2037**, extending its **Pirelli tyre-supply partnership to 2028**, and a new multi-year broadcast deal with Austria's ServusTV — as evidence the sport's underlying business remains healthy.
key_points: F1 owner **Liberty Media** reported Q2 2026 revenue of **$764 million**, down **38%** from $1.22 billion a year earlier.
**Operating income fell** from $293 million to just $73 million; adjusted profit (OIBDA) dropped **61%**.
The cause: only **5 races were held** in the quarter versus 9 a year earlier, after Middle East regional conflict forced postponements.
Total **viewing hours actually rose 13%**, undercutting any read that fans are tuning out.
Liberty struck new long-term deals anyway: the **Las Vegas GP through 2037**, **Pirelli through 2028**, and a new Austria broadcast deal.

depth.background: **Liberty Media** is the US company that owns and commercially runs Formula 1, and it reports F1's finances every quarter as part of its public earnings. F1's revenue comes mainly from race-hosting fees, broadcasting rights and sponsorship — so **fewer races directly means less revenue** in a given quarter, even if nothing is wrong with the sport's popularity. Earlier in 2026, regional conflict in the Middle East forced the postponement of several scheduled Grands Prix.

stories.title: Bangladesh's first Test tour of Australia in 23 years hits turbulence before it even starts, after a heavy warm-up defeat
stories.what_happened: Bangladesh's tour warm-up match against a Cricket Australia XI in Darwin exposed real gaps in their preparation: **Teague Wyllie scored 130**, with supporting half-centuries from Jake Doran and Kurtis Patterson, helping the CA XI build a substantial first-innings lead despite Bangladesh's Hasan Mahmud taking 4 for 42. Bangladesh's own batting then struggled badly in reply, slipping to **19 for 2** by the close as Campbell Thompson removed both Shadman Islam and Mominul Haque, and the tourists ultimately lost the warm-up **by an innings and 38 runs**. The first of two Tests begins in **Darwin on August 13**, with the second in **Mackay from August 22–26**, both counting toward the 2025–27 World Test Championship standings.
key_points: Bangladesh tour Australia for **Tests for the first time in 23 years**, opening in **Darwin on August 13**.
They lost their warm-up match to a **Cricket Australia XI by an innings and 38 runs**.
CA XI's **Teague Wyllie hit 130**, with fifties from Jake Doran and Kurtis Patterson, in the warm-up.
Bangladesh's second innings slipped to **19/2** by the close of the warm-up match.
The two-Test series (Darwin, then Mackay Aug 22–26) is part of the **2025–27 World Test Championship cycle**.

depth.background: Bangladesh have not played a Test match on Australian soil in **23 years**, making this tour a genuinely historic assignment against one of the sport's toughest opponents on its own turf — Australia is also playing its first home Tests since completing a **4–1 Ashes win over England**. The tour forms part of the ongoing **World Test Championship**, the league system that ranks Test-playing nations toward a biennial final, so results here carry ranking weight beyond just the series itself. Warm-up matches before a Test series exist precisely to let touring teams adjust to local conditions — pitch and ball behaviour that differ significantly from home — before matches that count.

stories.title: Cadillac gives up on its winless 2026 car to focus everything on 2027, as F1's newest team hits the summer break with zero points
stories.what_happened: Valtteri Bottas has confirmed that Cadillac will soon **halt development of its 2026 car** entirely and redirect its engineering resources toward the 2027 car instead. The team reaches the summer break as the only one on the grid without a single point, sitting **11th and last** in the constructors' championship after 11 races. Bottas's best result so far is **13th place** at the Chinese Grand Prix, and the car has suffered **five retirements** in the season's first half, including a brake fire during the Hungarian Grand Prix that was serious enough that Bottas has since stopped using the pit-entry wall approach during races. Separately, reports indicate American driver **Colton Herta**'s once-strong chances of landing a Cadillac F1 seat have largely evaporated as the team evaluates its options for future line-ups.
key_points: Cadillac will soon **stop developing its 2026 car** to pour resources into next year's, says driver Valtteri Bottas.
F1's newest team sits **11th and last** in the constructors' championship after 11 races, with **zero points**.
Bottas's best finish is **13th** (China), with **five retirements** in the first half of the season.
A brake fire in Hungary forced Bottas to stop using the **pit-entry wall**, a further sign of car reliability issues.
Colton Herta's reported chances of an F1 seat at Cadillac have **evaporated** as the team reviews driver options.

depth.background: Cadillac joined Formula 1 in 2026 as the sport's newest entrant, fielding an all-new team built largely from scratch — historically one of the hardest ways to compete in F1, since new teams typically need several seasons just to reach the development level of established rivals. The team paired experienced driver **Valtteri Bottas**, a former Mercedes and Alfa Romeo/Sauber driver with 10 grand prix wins, alongside Sergio Perez, hoping his experience would help bed in a brand-new car and organisation. Coming into the sport in the same year as a major new set of technical regulations added an extra layer of difficulty, since every team was starting fresh design work simultaneously.

stories.title: Ukraine advances near Kharkiv as Zelensky warns Russia is exploiting a near-total interceptor shortage
stories.what_happened: President Volodymyr Zelensky said this week that Ukraine is now receiving **almost three times fewer** anti-ballistic-missile interceptors than it was at the start of 2026, even as Russia keeps up large-scale missile and drone barrages. Analysts tracking the war say Russia may be deliberately timing the **start of its 2026-2027 winter strike campaign** for August specifically to exploit this gap while Ukraine's stockpiles are thin. Separately, Ukrainian forces reported a **fresh advance northeast of Kharkiv City** this week, one of the few reported territorial gains for Kyiv in recent weeks even as the broader front remains largely static. Zelensky renewed his call for allies to grant Ukraine a **license to manufacture Patriot interceptors domestically**, arguing that if the license had come earlier, Ukraine would already be producing interceptors **"for everyone, including Europe."** The interceptor crunch is compounded by global demand from the **2026 Iran war**, which is drawing on the same US production lines.
key_points: Zelensky says Ukraine is now getting **almost three times fewer** Patriot interceptor missiles than at the **start of 2026**
Ukrainian forces have made a **fresh advance northeast of Kharkiv City**, one of the few active gains reported this week
Analysts warn Russia may be timing a **new 2026-2027 strike campaign** for August specifically to exploit the interceptor gap
Zelensky is pushing allies for a **license to build Patriot interceptors domestically** in Ukraine, saying Kyiv could already be supplying **all of Europe** if it had received it sooner
The shortage stems partly from the **2026 Iran war** pulling on the same interceptor stockpiles allies would otherwise send to Ukraine

depth.background: Russia has leaned harder on long-range missile and drone barrages in 2026 as its ground offensive grinds forward slowly, and Ukraine has depended almost entirely on US-made **Patriot air-defense batteries** to stop the ballistic missiles that ordinary anti-air guns can't reach. On August 5, a Russian strike of 115 drones and 28 missiles hit Kyiv with **zero interceptions of any of the 28 missiles** — the first time in a while Ukraine's Patriot batteries came up completely empty. That shortage has only worsened since, even as Ukraine has managed a rare battlefield gain near Kharkiv, the northeastern city Russia has repeatedly tried and failed to encircle since 2022.

thread.previously: On August 5-6 we reported that Russia's biggest strike on Kyiv in weeks killed 17 people after Ukraine's Patriot batteries intercepted zero of 28 incoming missiles, exposing a critical interceptor shortage.
thread.changed: Zelensky has now quantified the shortfall — almost three times fewer interceptors than earlier in 2026 — and warned Russia may be timing a full autumn strike campaign to exploit it, even as Ukraine posts a rare battlefield gain near Kharkiv.

stories.title: Gabriel Bortoleto says Audi's F1 project is a totally different operation than the Sauber team he joined
stories.what_happened: Speaking to media, Bortoleto said the reality — the **"truth"** — is that Audi's full takeover has changed the team into something completely different from the Sauber outfit he originally signed with, citing the scale of investment and structural change since Audi's backing arrived. He praised the chassis Audi's engineers have built for its **debut F1 season**, calling it **"very strong,"** but was candid that the **power unit** side of the project still has work to do, since Audi is in just its first year of building an F1 engine compared to manufacturers who've been doing it for **15 years** under the previous hybrid rules. Despite the early engine shortfall, Bortoleto expressed confidence Audi will eventually become one of the sport's top engine manufacturers, and confirmed that his own future with the team is **already locked in** under a multi-year contract.
key_points: Bortoleto says the **"truth"** is that Audi's takeover has made the team an **entirely different operation** from the Sauber squad he originally signed with
He believes Audi has built a **"very strong"** first F1 chassis, even in year one
He acknowledges the **engine side still needs work** — Audi is only in its **first year** building a power unit while rivals have had **15 years**
Bortoleto's **long-term future with Audi is already settled** under a **multi-year contract**
He expects Audi will eventually become **one of the top engine manufacturers** in F1

depth.background: Audi has been building toward a full factory entry in Formula 1 for years, taking a phased approach: it first took a stake in the Sauber team before formally becoming Audi's works team under the 2026 power-unit rules, which also reset the engine competition across the whole grid. Gabriel Bortoleto, a rising young Brazilian driver, joined the Sauber pipeline before the Audi transition was complete and is now one of the team's two race drivers under the new Audi identity.

stories.title: A total solar eclipse will darken skies over Iceland and Spain on August 12 — Europe's first since 1999
stories.what_happened: On **August 12, 2026**, the Moon's shadow will sweep across the Arctic and North Atlantic before crossing western **Iceland** and the northern half of **Spain and Portugal**, delivering full darkness in daytime for up to **2 minutes 18 seconds** at the path's widest point. The eclipse begins over remote northern Russia near the North Pole, crosses Greenland and Iceland in the late afternoon, and reaches Spain in the evening, just before sunset. Because the path passes mostly over ocean and sparsely populated Arctic land, Iceland and Spain are the two realistic viewing hubs, and both are bracing for an influx of visitors. Observers across the **UK and Ireland**, outside the path of totality, will still see a dramatic partial eclipse with roughly **90%** of the Sun blotted out. NASA, the European Space Agency and national observatories have published detailed path maps ahead of the event.
key_points: The path of totality crosses Greenland, Iceland and northern Spain on **August 12**, lasting up to **2 minutes 18 seconds**.
It's the **first total solar eclipse visible from mainland Europe since 1999** — a 27-year wait.
The UK and Ireland get a deep **partial eclipse**, with up to **90% of the Sun covered**.
In Spain and Portugal the eclipse hits during the **golden hour**, just before sunset.
Iceland and northern Spain are bracing for a **surge of eclipse-chasing tourists** in the coming days.

depth.background: Total solar eclipses happen when the Moon passes directly between the Sun and Earth, fully blocking sunlight along a narrow strip called the **path of totality** — outside that path, viewers see only a partial eclipse. Mainland Europe has been eclipse-starved: the last total eclipse visible there was in **1999**, so an entire generation has never seen one from home soil. This eclipse's path threads a mostly-ocean route from the Arctic down through Iceland and into Spain, meaning very few people live directly in its shadow, which is exactly why astronomers, airlines and tourism boards have spent months preparing.

stories.title: Honda declares its target is to make Fernando Alonso F1 champion again, as Aston Martin's upgrade pays off
stories.what_happened: Honda Racing Corporation president **Koji Watanabe** said explicitly that Honda's target with Aston Martin is "to become world champion from 2026 onwards," a public commitment to making Fernando Alonso competitive again. The statement follows a difficult start to Aston Martin's 2026 season, after which the team and Honda introduced a package of **16 upgrades** to the car at the **Hungarian Grand Prix**. The upgrades appeared to work: both Alonso and teammate **Lance Stroll** posted their **season-high finishes**, 14th and 13th respectively. Despite the improvement, Alonso's future remains unresolved — he has said he will decide after the summer break whether to stay at Aston Martin, and has been openly critical of F1's new 2026 regulations, with reports suggesting he could be eyeing a move to Alpine for 2027 instead.
key_points: Honda Racing Corporation president **Koji Watanabe** declared Honda's target is "**to become world champion from 2026 onwards**" with Alonso.
Aston Martin and Honda introduced a **16-part upgrade package** at the **Hungarian Grand Prix**.
The upgrades delivered **season-high finishes** — **Alonso 14th**, teammate **Lance Stroll 13th**.
Alonso will decide **after the summer break** whether he stays at Aston Martin, or in F1 at all.
Alonso has criticized F1's **2026 regulations** and has reportedly been linked to a possible **Alpine** move for 2027.

depth.background: Fernando Alonso, a two-time F1 world champion, joined Aston Martin in 2023 partly on the promise that the team's new Honda engine partnership, starting in 2026, would eventually make it a title contender. Aston Martin's 2026 season started poorly, putting that promise under pressure, and Alonso — now in his mid-40s — has made clear he's unhappy with this year's new technical regulations. Honda, as the team's engine supplier, has a direct stake in proving the partnership can deliver, since a struggling car reflects on the engine as much as the chassis.

stories.title: Mercedes braces for 'almost inevitable' grid penalties for Antonelli and Russell as engine parts run out
stories.what_happened: Mercedes has acknowledged that grid penalties for both **Kimi Antonelli** and **George Russell** are now "almost inevitable" in the second half of the 2026 season, after a run of power-unit reliability problems. Both drivers are already using their **fourth internal combustion engine**, **third energy store** and **third control electronics** — parts for which the FIA allocates a limited number per season before a penalty applies. Exceeding the allowance for even one element triggers a **10-place grid penalty** the first time it happens, and if a team changes multiple parts for the same race, a driver can be sent to the **back of the grid** entirely. Mercedes is reportedly considering **Monza**, Antonelli's home Italian Grand Prix, as one option to absorb the penalty. The situation is especially high-stakes because both drivers are currently fighting for the championship, so wherever Mercedes takes the hit could affect the title fight.
key_points: Mercedes accepts penalties for **Kimi Antonelli** and **George Russell** are now "**almost inevitable**" in the season's second half.
Both drivers are already on their **fourth internal combustion engine**, third energy store and third control electronics.
Exceeding one engine-part allocation triggers a **10-place grid drop**; multiple parts replaced together can send a driver to the **back of the grid**.
Mercedes is weighing **Monza**, Antonelli's home race, as the venue to absorb the penalty.
Both drivers are currently in the thick of the **2026 title fight**, so the timing could swing the championship.

depth.background: F1 cars run a "power unit" — engine, energy store and electronics — and each driver is allowed only a limited number of each part per season before penalties apply, a rule meant to control costs and reliability spending. Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli and George Russell have both suffered power-unit reliability issues and race-ending failures this year, forcing the team to dip into replacement parts earlier than planned. Because engine penalties apply as grid-position drops at a race of the team's choosing, teams try to time them for a circuit where track position matters less.

stories.title: Top US CENTCOM commander makes a snap visit to Israel to assess the multi-front standoff with Iran, Lebanon and Gaza
stories.what_happened: Adm. Brad Cooper arrived in Israel on **August 8** and held a security assessment with IDF Chief of Staff **Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir** and other senior Israeli commanders, according to Israeli and regional outlets. The visit followed stops in **Bahrain and the United Arab Emirates**, part of what appears to be a broader regional check-in. The IDF said the meeting reinforced the **'close strategic relationship'** between the two militaries, while reports described the discussion as centered on the current 'multi-front' picture — the shaky Gaza ceasefire, the standoff with Iran, and the risk of escalation with Hezbollah in Lebanon. The visit landed alongside notably upbeat comments from Iran's president and the US vice president about the prospects of a fresh ceasefire framework, though no deal was announced.
key_points: US Central Command chief **Adm. Brad Cooper** met Israel's military chief **Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir** in Israel on August 8.
The visit came right after Cooper held talks in **Bahrain and the UAE**, suggesting a regional security tour.
Officials described it as an assessment of the **'multi-front' situation** — Gaza, Lebanon/Hezbollah, and Iran all at once.
It coincided with **cautiously optimistic remarks** from Iran's president and the US vice president about a possible new ceasefire track.
The IDF called it evidence of a **'close strategic relationship'** between the US and Israeli militaries.

depth.background: CENTCOM is the US military command responsible for the Middle East, and its chief visiting Israel in person — rather than by video call — is typically read as a signal of how seriously Washington is tracking the region's multiple, overlapping conflicts: the Gaza ceasefire's fragile second phase, ongoing tension with Iran, and the risk of a wider flare-up involving Hezbollah in Lebanon. Adm. Cooper has made several such regional trips in 2026 as the US has tried to keep a lid on any one of these fronts spiraling into a bigger war.

stories.title: Spain hits back at Italy with retaliatory border checks in an escalating EU migration feud
stories.what_happened: Italy moved first: from **August 1**, it began checking Spanish citizens arriving by air and sea and formally suspended Spain's Schengen rights, the EU rule that normally lets citizens move between 29 member countries without passport checks. Rome framed the move as a response to the Ceuta migrant surge. Spain gave Italy until **August 9** to lift its checks or face "proportionate measures." When Meloni refused, Madrid followed through: from midnight Saturday, travellers arriving from Italy face **random checks at Spanish ports and airports**, under a decree that runs until at least September 7. Sánchez has pushed back publicly, arguing Italy itself has recorded more irregular border crossings than Spain in recent years, and that "respect for European treaties and the facts is not optional."
key_points: Spain began **random police checks on Italian travellers** at its ports and airports from midnight Saturday, running until at least **September 7**.
It's a **tit-for-tat response**: Italy had already suspended Spain's Schengen free-movement rights on **August 1**, checking Spanish travellers by air and sea.
The trigger was a **record ~72,000-migrant surge** into Spain's North African enclave of **Ceuta** late last month, in which **more than 80 people died**.
Italy's PM Giorgia Meloni criticised Spain's migrant amnesty policy; Spain's PM Pedro Sánchez says Italy has recorded **more irregular entries** than Spain since 2021.
The **Schengen zone** — Europe's passport-free travel area covering 29 countries — is being selectively suspended between two of its own founding-era members.

depth.background: Ceuta is a small Spanish territory on Morocco's coast, and it periodically becomes a flashpoint when large numbers of migrants attempt to cross into it as a gateway to mainland Europe. Late last month roughly 72,000 people rushed the border in one of the largest such surges on record; most were later sent back, but Spanish and Moroccan authorities say over 80 people died, some drowned or trampled while trying to cross a breakwater barrier. The crisis has become a proxy fight over EU migration policy between Spain's socialist government, which recently granted residency status to some undocumented migrants already in the country, and Italy's hard-right government, which has long pushed for stricter EU-wide migration rules.

stories.title: Iran and Oman agree shipping-lane coordinates for the Strait of Hormuz as a deal nears completion
stories.what_happened: Iranian Foreign Minister **Abbas Araghchi** said Saturday that Tehran's agreement with Oman on managing traffic through the Strait of Hormuz is "**very close**." Negotiators have spent more than **three weeks** working out the details and have now agreed on the actual shipping routes: inbound vessels will travel a **northern lane through Iranian territorial waters**, while outbound vessels will use a **southern lane in Omani waters**, coordinated with Iran. The two sides are also finalizing a **joint coordination center** to manage maritime traffic and collect information on vessels passing through. Despite the progress, Araghchi cautioned that a full, unrestricted reopening of the strait still depends on the United States honoring commitments it made in a **June memorandum of understanding** — which Iran says Washington has already violated.
key_points: Iran and Oman have agreed on the **exact shipping-lane coordinates** through the Strait of Hormuz after **three weeks** of talks
Inbound tankers will use a **northern lane through Iranian waters**; outbound cargo runs through a **southern lane in Omani waters**
Iran's foreign minister called the agreement "**very close**" but says a full reopening still depends on the **US honoring a June memorandum**
A **joint coordination center** would track vessel traffic and gather information from ships transiting the strait
The strait carries roughly **a fifth of the world's oil** — any resolution here directly moves global energy prices

depth.background: Since the 2026 Iran war escalated, the **Strait of Hormuz** — the narrow waterway between Iran and Oman that a huge share of the world's seaborne oil must pass through — has been repeatedly targeted, with multiple tankers hit by missiles and drones this year. **Oman**, a neutral broker with ties to both Tehran and Washington, has spent weeks mediating a technical arrangement to keep commercial shipping moving safely through the strait. The talks gained urgency after the **US revoked a license** permitting Iranian oil sales and after a **June memorandum of understanding**, meant to de-escalate the wider war, ran into trouble.

thread.previously: On August 7 we reported that Iran and Oman's Hormuz shipping deal had entered final drafting, reportedly on terms favorable to Iran.
thread.changed: Iran's foreign minister now says the deal is "very close," with the actual shipping-lane coordinates agreed — though a full reopening still hinges on the US honoring a disputed June memorandum.

stories.title: Trent Rockets Women clinch Hundred knockout qualification with a dominant 9-wicket rout of MI London
stories.what_happened: Trent Rockets Women demolished MI London Women by **9 wickets** at Kennington Oval, their fifth consecutive win of the campaign. Chasing MI London's total, **Nat Sciver-Brunt made an unbeaten 67 off just 36 balls** and **Beth Mooney finished on 54 not out off 44 balls**, taking Trent Rockets home with overs to spare. The result mathematically **secures Trent Rockets' place in the knockout stage**, making them one of the first two teams — alongside Southern Brave — to lock in a top finish in the women's competition, while several other sides are still fighting for the remaining spots.
key_points: Trent Rockets Women beat MI London Women by **9 wickets**, their **fifth straight win** in the competition.
The win **clinches their qualification** for The Hundred's knockout stage.
**Nat Sciver-Brunt (67 not out off 36 balls)** and **Beth Mooney (54 not out off 44 balls)** blitzed the chase.
Trent Rockets now sit among the **frontrunners** in the women's competition as the group stage nears its end.
It's the clearest form line yet in a women's table that's still being decided elsewhere in the competition.

depth.background: The Hundred's group stage runs eight matches per team, with the top-placed side in each of the men's and women's competitions going straight to the final at Lord's on August 16, while second and third play an eliminator at The Oval on August 14 for the second final spot. Trent Rockets Women have been one of the standout sides of the 2026 season, building form heading into the business end of the competition.

stories.title: Pakistan's Test squad flies to England after drawing the West Indies series, as Root's England side name Cox and Lawrence
stories.what_happened: Pakistan's Test squad departed the West Indies for England following their drawn two-Test series, in which the sides split the results 1-1 with Babar Azam returning as captain. Before the first Test against England on **August 19**, Pakistan will play a four-day warm-up match against a Select XI to adapt to English pitches and conditions. Pakistan's squad includes four uncapped players in contention for their first Test caps, plus batter Saud Shakeel pending a fitness test. On the home side, England — captained by **Joe Root** — have named their squad with **Jordan Cox** handed the No. 3 batting spot and **Dan Lawrence** recalled after scoring 788 runs at an average of 65.66 in the County Championship this season, including five centuries.
key_points: Pakistan's Test squad has **left the West Indies for England**, after the two-Test series there finished **1-1**.
The first Pakistan-England Test begins **August 19**, preceded by a four-day warm-up against a Select XI.
**Babar Azam** returns as Pakistan's Test captain, replacing the sacked Shan Masood.
England, led by **Joe Root**, have handed **Jordan Cox** one of the biggest opportunities of his career at No. 3.
**Dan Lawrence** is recalled after a huge County Championship season — 788 runs at an average of 65.66 for Surrey.

depth.background: Pakistan toured the West Indies for a two-Test series that ended level at 1-1, giving Babar Azam — reinstated as Test captain after Shan Masood was sacked — a winning start in his second stint in charge. Pakistan now moves straight into a three-match Test series in England, part of the ongoing World Test Championship cycle, with the first Test starting August 19 after a warm-up match to adjust to English conditions.

stories.title: Red Bull's Mekies signals Isack Hadjar will stay on as Verstappen's teammate beyond 2026
stories.what_happened: Red Bull team principal **Laurent Mekies** said in recent comments that Isack Hadjar is 'performing solidly' and has 'learned a lot from the team and from Max,' adding: **'It is good news that we have a strong second driver for the first time in quite a long time.'** While not a formal contract announcement, the comments are widely read in the paddock as confirmation that Hadjar will remain Verstappen's teammate beyond 2026, with an official extension expected to follow. This lands alongside separate reports that Red Bull has tabled an improved contract for Verstappen himself, suggesting the team wants to lock in both drivers together.
key_points: Red Bull boss **Laurent Mekies** strongly hinted Isack Hadjar will remain in the senior team past this season.
Mekies called having a **'strong second driver'** alongside Max Verstappen **'good news'** for the team.
Hadjar, 21, races on a **contract reviewed annually**, and a formal extension is now expected.
This comes as Red Bull separately offered Verstappen an **improved contract**, tying down its two-driver lineup.
It removes one seat from F1's crowded **2027 driver market**, where several other seats remain contested.

depth.background: Isack Hadjar was promoted to partner Max Verstappen at Red Bull's senior team from the start of the 2026 season under what's been described as a '1+1' deal with performance clauses, reviewed annually rather than locked in for multiple years. Red Bull has a history of being ruthless with driver seats — several drivers, including Hadjar's now-teammate Liam Lawson, have been dropped from the senior team mid-contract in recent years, so any signal of stability is notable.

stories.title: Liam Lawson says he's 'in a good place' after a career-best first half of the 2026 F1 season
stories.what_happened: Lawson has scored points at **8 of the 11 grand prix** held so far in 2026, putting him **9th in the drivers' standings** — a marked improvement on his troubled 2025. Speaking about his form, Lawson said: **'When you're in a good rhythm and you find things that are working for you, it's obviously a good feeling'** and that the results have put him in **'a good place.'** He attributes the turnaround to a full season of preparation and experience in a stable seat, after having to recover from the embarrassment of his early-2025 Red Bull demotion. Racing Bulls' car has been competitive under 2026's new rules, regularly finishing inside the points.
key_points: Lawson has scored points in **8 of 11 races** so far in 2026, sitting **9th** in the drivers' championship.
It's a sharp turnaround from a year ago, when he was **demoted out of Red Bull's senior team** early in the 2025 season.
He credits better **preparation and rhythm** in a full-time seat at Racing Bulls, Red Bull's junior team.
Racing Bulls' car has **frequently featured inside the top 10** in this new regulation cycle.
Lawson says the results this year are letting him drive with more confidence than at any point in his career.

depth.background: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand driver who was promoted to Red Bull's senior team for the start of 2025, only to be demoted back to the junior team, **Racing Bulls**, after a rocky start — a very public setback in F1's brutal driver pecking order. 2026 marked the start of a new F1 technical regulation cycle, which reshuffled the competitive order across the grid and gave several midfield teams, including Racing Bulls, a more competitive car.

stories.title: India presses China for transparency on its Brahmaputra mega-dam at fresh border talks, even as the Arunachal naming row simmers
stories.what_happened: Indian and Chinese diplomats met in New Delhi for the 36th WMCC meeting, with India represented by Joint Secretary (East Asia) **Sujit Ghosh** and China by **Hou Yanqi**, Director General of the Boundary and Oceanic Affairs Department. India used the meeting to press China for **greater transparency** about its upstream hydropower construction on trans-border rivers, and called for an early meeting of the expert-level mechanism on hydrological data-sharing — a long-standing Indian concern given China's control over the river's headwaters. The two sides also reviewed the LAC situation, including developments specifically in Arunachal Pradesh, and agreed to keep relying on established diplomatic and military channels to manage the border and avoid fresh flare-ups, without announcing any new breakthrough.
key_points: India and China held the **36th round** of their Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination (WMCC) on border affairs in New Delhi
India pressed Beijing for **greater transparency** on its upstream hydropower projects on rivers flowing into India
China's planned mega-dam on the **Yarlung Tsangpo** — which becomes the Siang, then the Brahmaputra, in India — is reported to cost roughly **$147 billion**
Both sides also discussed the **Line of Actual Control (LAC)** situation, specifically around Arunachal Pradesh
They agreed to keep using existing diplomatic and military channels to prevent fresh tension, without resolving the underlying dispute

depth.background: India and China have fought no full war since 1962, but their **3,488-km Line of Actual Control (LAC)** — the de facto, undemarcated border — remains a running source of friction, sharpened by a deadly 2020 clash in Ladakh's Galwan Valley. Since then, the two sides have used the **WMCC**, a diplomat-level forum, to manage day-to-day frictions while broader boundary talks proceed separately at a more senior level. A newer flashpoint has emerged over water: China is building a giant hydropower project on the Yarlung Tsangpo river in Tibet, just before it crosses into Arunachal Pradesh and becomes the Siang and then the Brahmaputra — a river tens of millions of Indians in India's northeast and Bangladesh depend on downstream.

thread.previously: India's Home Ministry formally renamed 27 places in Arunachal Pradesh on official maps on August 7, directly countering China's own renaming campaign in the disputed state — a low-cost administrative assertion of its territorial claim.
thread.changed: Just two days later, the two countries' diplomats sat down anyway for the 36th round of WMCC border talks, where India pressed China on transparency for its huge Brahmaputra-basin mega-dam and both sides discussed the Arunachal Pradesh LAC situation directly, agreeing to keep using existing channels rather than let the naming dispute derail routine border management.

stories.title: Delhi Police roll out multi-layered Independence Day security amid Khalistani-threat warnings
stories.what_happened: Delhi Police have implemented a **comprehensive, multi-layered security strategy** for this year's Independence Day events at the Red Fort, including coordination meetings with central security agencies and intelligence units. The stepped-up measures include closer monitoring of **suspicious movements** and heightened **surveillance on hotels, guest houses and crowded public places** across the capital, driven partly by concerns over potential disruption from Khalistani operatives that Indian officials allege are backed by Pakistan's ISI. In parallel, security has also been tightened in **Rajouri**, Jammu & Kashmir, covering both the ongoing **Baba Budha Amarnath Yatra** (an annual Hindu pilgrimage) and the run-up to Independence Day, with **CRPF, CISF, and Jammu & Kashmir Police** deployed at key locations in the sector.
key_points: Delhi Police held coordination meetings with central agencies ahead of **August 15** celebrations at the Red Fort.
Security concerns cite possible threats from **Khalistani operatives** allegedly backed by Pakistan's **ISI**.
Surveillance has been stepped up on **hotels, guest houses and crowded public places** across the capital.

CRPF, CISF and J&K Police have been deployed at key locations in the Rajouri sector.

depth.background: India's Independence Day, marked every August 15 with the Prime Minister's address from the Red Fort, is treated as one of the country's highest-security public events every year, given its symbolic importance and history as a target for threats. Security planning typically escalates in the weeks before, coordinating Delhi Police with central paramilitary forces and intelligence agencies. Threats attributed to 'Khalistani' networks — separatist groups seeking an independent Sikh state, which India accuses Pakistan's intelligence agency (the ISI) of covertly supporting — are a recurring theme in India's domestic security assessments, especially around high-profile national events.

stories.title: India stays silent as US Senate's Russia sanctions bill puts trade talks and energy security on a collision course
stories.what_happened: The **US Senate passed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 86-11 on Friday, August 7**, authorizing the president to impose secondary tariffs of up to 100% on countries that keep buying large volumes of Russian oil and gas unless they sharply cut purchases. India and China, which together buy roughly 70% of Russia's energy export revenue, are the bill's clear main targets. As of **Saturday, August 8**, Indian officials have made **no formal public statement** reacting to the bill's passage. Trade analysts note the vote **complicates the ongoing US-India bilateral trade talks**, since Washington now holds fresh leverage over New Delhi heading into further negotiating rounds. India has previously insisted its Russian oil purchases are about ensuring stable energy supply amid volatile global markets, not a political choice to support Moscow.
key_points: New Delhi has made **no public comment** on the Senate bill threatening up to **100% tariffs** on Russian-oil buyers.
The bill lands in the middle of **ongoing US-India trade negotiations**, giving Washington fresh leverage.
India defends its Russian crude purchases as **energy security**, not war funding, rejecting the US framing.
The bill grants the president **discretion, not a mandate** — Trump hasn't said whether he'd actually impose the tariffs on India.
The bill next goes to the **House**, expected to act after its recess ends around **August 31**.

depth.background: India has sharply increased purchases of discounted Russian crude oil since 2022, when Western sanctions on Russia pushed prices down and many traditional buyers pulled back. India argues this is simply smart energy-security policy for a country that imports most of its oil. The US has periodically criticized this as indirectly funding Russia's war in Ukraine, and separately, Washington and New Delhi have been negotiating a bilateral trade agreement covering tariffs on Indian exports — talks that were already tense before this bill passed.

thread.previously: The Senate passed the Graham Act 86-11, authorizing the president to impose up to 100% secondary tariffs on major buyers of Russian energy, with China and India as the main targets, but leaving enforcement to Trump's discretion.
thread.changed: A day later, India has made no public response, and analysts say the bill now complicates the separate, ongoing US-India bilateral trade talks by giving Washington extra leverage.
